text:
@BarackObama found a principle.

He says the government can't target people for "what they say." In 2010, his Justice Department got a judge to sign a warrant for a Fox News reporter's email and called him a possible co-conspirator.

For asking questions. I graded all of it.

His screenshot is attached with my red pen in the margins. This is the long version, because a man who carried the nuclear football for eight years can handle a long version. Grab a coffee, Barry. Grab two. You're going to be here a while.

— LINE ONE: "A BASIC PRINCIPLE OF AMERICAN DEMOCRACY" —

Barry. You taught constitutional law at the University of Chicago. The word "democracy" appears in the Constitution exactly zero times. Article IV, Section 4 guarantees every state "a Republican Form of Government." Slight oversight! Somewhere a law school wants its lecture notes back.

But fine. Let's grade the principle itself: the government can't selectively target people because of their political beliefs or what they say.

Agreed. Now open your own transcript.

May 2010. Your Justice Department applied for a warrant to search the personal email of James Rosen, Fox News' chief Washington correspondent. The FBI affidavit claimed probable cause that he broke the Espionage Act "as an aider and abettor and/or co-conspirator." His offense? Asking a State Department source for information. That is called journalism. A magistrate signed it. NBC reported Eric Holder signed off. Rosen was never charged.

I swore an oath to support and defend the Constitution against all enemies, foreign and domestic. Nobody handed me a list of which Americans it covered. The First Amendment doesn't come with a footnote that says "except Fox." You swore to preserve, protect and defend that same Constitution. Twice. Apparently your copy came with an asterisk.

May 2013. The Associated Press learned your Justice Department had secretly pulled the records of 20 of its phone lines covering April and May of 2012.

Same month, the Treasury Inspector General reported your IRS had used inappropriate criteria to flag tax-exempt applications with words like "Tea Party" and "Patriot" in the name. Lois Lerner took the Fifth in front of Congress. Nine months later you sat across from Bill O'Reilly and said there wasn't "even a smidgen of corruption." In October 2017 the IRS settled with those groups and formally apologized.

To be fair, a later review found some progressive keywords got flagged too. The conservative list still did the heavy lifting. A smidgen, you said. You've got a leak in the think tank, sir, and the whole library is flooding.

There's an old word for a shrewd, unprincipled politician who preaches what he never practiced. Snollygoster. Look it up. Your picture should be next to it.

— LINE TWO: "IT'S IMPORTANT TO KNOW THE FACTS" —

He actually wrote that. The man who told 300 million Americans "if you like your plan, you can keep your plan," which PolitiFact named its Lie of the Year in 2013. Facts matter to Barack Obama about as much as a seat belt matters to a crash-test dummy. They're strapped in for the photo, and they go flying the second the car hits something.

I was a paramedic for twenty years. I know what it looks like when somebody presents with one story and the vitals tell another. Keep talking, Barry. I'm diagnosing your condition. It's called selective memory, and it's chronic.

His facts: Omar arrived at 12. Five years later her father naturalized. She was 17, so she became a citizen automatically.

Here are the facts he left on the cutting-room floor.

The Minnesota Legislative Reference Library listed her birth year as 1981. It said 1981 for her entire time in the state House. In May 2019, months into her first term in Congress, her staff asked the library to change it to 1982. The library's own director put that request in writing.

Born in 1981, she's 18 or 19 when her father naturalized in 2000, and an 18-year-old has to apply on her own. Born in 1982, she's 17 and rides in on Dad's paperwork.

One digit. That is the entire citizenship.

I teach physics. One digit is the difference between a bridge that holds and a bridge that drops a school bus into the river. Nobody in my classroom gets to say "close enough" about a decimal, and nobody in Congress gets to say it about a birth year.

She says the old year was a mistake. Possible. Refugees from war zones often don't have clean birth records, and immigration lawyers say so. So produce the records, Congresswoman. The father's certificate. The file. A former congressional candidate, AJ Kern, requested his naturalization records and posted the reply from USCIS: no matching index reference under the name variants she gave. A failed records search is not proof he never naturalized. It IS a reason not to announce it as settled fact to 6.9 million people, Mr. President.

— LINE THREE: "AN UNSUBSTANTIATED THEORY" —

Here's what substantiated looks like.

A federal judge read an affidavit and found probable cause before agents walked through her door on October 12. The Justice Department confirmed the warrant was "judicially authorized." AP reports more than a dozen grand jury subpoenas, some to her own relatives, for a grand jury in Minnesota. Tom Homan said on Fox he's been told it's a "strong case." Jonathan Turley pointed out the civil denaturalization track has no statute of limitations.

Unsubstantiated theories don't get a judge's signature, a grand jury, and a stack of subpoenas. Calling that "unsubstantiated" is like calling the Titanic a little damp. You're muddying the water to make it look deep, and the whole country can see the bottom.

To be fair, her lawyers say agents ignored limits a judge put on the search, and they want her property back. If agents broke the judge's rules, that's a real problem and I'll say so out loud. Notice what that complaint admits, though. A judge was in charge of this the whole time.

And that same night, her campaign sent a fundraising email asking supporters to "chip in." Persecuted all the way to the bank.

— LINE FOUR: "A NONEXISTENT SMOKING GUN FROM 20 YEARS AGO" —

Two errors in one sentence. I'm a teacher. I circle both.

Nonexistent? You don't know that. You haven't read the affidavit. Neither have I. The difference is I'm not the one who typed "nonexistent" in front of 6.9 million people.

Twenty years ago? Her father naturalized in 2000. It's 2026. That's twenty-six years. President of the Harvard Law Review, and the arithmetic still came out like a gas station receipt in the rain. My freshmen get partial credit for showing their work. You didn't show any. Somewhere a calculator is producing correct answers for you, sir. You owe it an apology.

— LINE FIVE: "BECAUSE SHE HAS DARED TO CRITICIZE THE PRESIDENT" —

What's next, Barry, you'll tell me Biden's own people looked at her first... wait, I'm being told.

The Wall Street Journal reported Homeland Security Investigations examined a similar allegation under Biden's Autopen and dropped it for lack of evidence. The New York Times reported Biden's Justice Department opened a separate probe in June 2024 into her finances, her campaign spending, and her contact with a foreign national. It stalled. Even CNN's Elie Honig said the Biden-era start hurts her "selective and vindictive" argument.

So which president was she criticizing in June 2024 that scared his own Justice Department? Your old vice president? Take your time. You've got a presidential library with no presidential library in it. Plenty of quiet. Unless your name is Google, stop acting like you know everything about a case you've never read.

Let me propose the Obama Rule, since you seem to want one. Any American who criticizes the sitting president is immune from federal investigation. Criticize the president, skip the IRS. Criticize the president, skip the grand jury. Half of cable news and every member of the Squad, untouchable forever. This is not a radical idea. It's just common sense.

— LINE SIX: "DISMISSED FOR HAVING NO BASIS IN LAW" —

He offers the New York attorney general and the former FBI director as proof that Trump's Justice Department only brings junk cases.

On November 24, 2025, Judge Cameron Currie threw out the Comey and Letitia James indictments because Lindsey Halligan's appointment as U.S. attorney was unlawful. Without prejudice. That ruling was about who signed the indictment, not about what Comey or James did. To be fair, grand juries twice declined to re-indict James after that. That is a real point for your side. "No basis in law" is still your spin, not the judge's finding.

And since we're grading consistency: prosecutors in Manhattan, Georgia, and Biden's Autopen Justice Department indicted a former president four times in 2023, while he was running. Let me find the 400-word post where you warned that this could become the new normal. Looking... Looking... Oh. It's this one. Three years late and aimed the other way.

Quinn's Law Number Seven: it's different when you're a Democrat.

— THE PART HE REALLY DOESN'T WANT GRADED —

July 2016. Your FBI opened Crossfire Hurricane. It used Christopher Steele's dossier, paid for through the Clinton campaign and the DNC, to get four FISA warrants on Carter Page, an American citizen.

December 2019. The DOJ Inspector General found 17 significant errors and omissions in those applications. The Justice Department later conceded the last two lacked probable cause. An FBI lawyer altered an email and pleaded guilty. Steele's own primary sub-source told the FBI in January 2017 that much of it was hearsay and talk over beers. The IG didn't find documented bias in the opening. He also told the Senate his findings didn't vindicate anybody who touched it.

December 9, 2016. Per documents DNI Tulsi Gabbard declassified in July 2025, your top national security officials met at the White House, and a new intelligence assessment was ordered "per the President's request." To be fair, a bipartisan 2020 Senate Intelligence report still backed that assessment's finding that Russia interfered. Nobody disputes who requested it. The email subject line names you.

May 2020. A recording of your private call leaked. You said there was "no precedent" for someone charged with perjury getting off scot-free, talking about Michael Flynn. Flynn was never charged with perjury. He was charged with making false statements. Different statute. You taught this. A law professor who can't tell perjury from a false statement is like a fire chief who can't tell smoke from steam. The lights are on, Barry, but the power bill is overdue.

Matthew 7:5, LSB: "You hypocrite, first take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother's eye." Jesus said that to people who loved pointing at specks. You don't have a log, Mr. President. You have a lumberyard.

— THE GRADE —

o "Basic principle of American democracy." We're a republic, and your own Justice Department named a reporter a co-conspirator for asking questions.

o "Important to know the facts." Left out the 1981 birth year, the 2019 change request, and the Biden-era probes.

o "Unsubstantiated theory." Judge-approved warrant, Minnesota grand jury, a dozen-plus subpoenas.

o "20 years ago." Twenty-six. Show your work.

o "Because she dared to criticize the president." Biden's own people looked first.

o "No basis in law." Thrown out over an appointment, not the merits.

Final grade: F. Not an F for effort. An F for memory.

You end by warning that if this becomes the new normal, future presidents of either party will do the same. Sir, that isn't a warning about a precedent. That's your résumé read out loud.

Here's what actually makes me angry, and it isn't you. It's the kids.

I teach in a district the system gave up on. My students watch this stuff. They hear a former president of the United States say a judge-signed warrant is persecution, and they learn that the rules only count when your team loses. Then I'm the one who has to stand in front of them and explain that the law is supposed to work the same for a congresswoman, a Fox reporter, and a kid from my classroom. You made my job harder today. Thanks for that.

You campaign like a rock star and govern like a wet paper bag. You're all hat and no cattle on the rule of law. You're the hood ornament on the clown car, and the car's on fire. And you've got miles to go before you reach mediocre on consistency, Barry.

— THE CHALLENGE —

@BarackObama, I'm not asking you to agree with me. I'm asking you to grade me back.

Pick any line in this post. One. Show me where I got a fact wrong, with a source, and I will post the correction myself with your name on it. No spin, no excuses. That's what a teacher does when he's wrong.

And while you're at it, answer one question for the people who still listen to you: if a judge-signed warrant on Ilhan Omar is persecution, what was a judge-signed warrant on James Rosen's email?

Better yet, come defend your post in front of my students. Third period. I'll even let you use notes. They're teenagers, and I promise they'll go easier on you than the facts did.

I'll wait. I've got grading.

So, Obama fans: if Trump's Justice Department had called a CNN reporter a possible co-conspirator for asking questions, what would you be calling it right now?

But what do I know, I'm only a science teacher who reads the affidavit before he grades the press release.

2:223: "Your wives are a place of sowing of seed for you, so come to your place of cultivation however you wish and put forth [righteousness] for yourselves. And fear Allah and know that you will meet Him. And give good tidings to the believers"   

- Demands obedience to Allah and His messenger, declaring that Allah has no love for those who turn away in disbelief.

3:32: "Say, "Obey Allah and the Messenger." But if they turn away - then indeed, Allah does not like the disbelievers."

- Declares that terror will be struck into the hearts of polytheists for worshiping other entities without divine sanction, consigning them to Hell.

3:151: "We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve for what they have associated with Allah of which He had not sent down [any] authority. And their refuge will be the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers."

- Permits men to marry up to four women, or restrict themselves to one wife or enslaved concubines if they fear they cannot treat multiple wives equitably.

4:3: "And if you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry (other) women of your choice, two or three, or four but if you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly (with them), then only one or (the captives and the slaves) that your right hands possess. That is nearer to prevent you from doing injustice."   

- Prohibits marriage to women who are already married, with an explicit exception made for female captives/enslaved women owned by believers.

4:24: "You are forbidden to marry married women except your slave-girls. This is the decree of God. Besides these, it is lawful for you to marry other women if you pay their dower, maintain chastity and do not commit indecency. If you marry them for the appointed time you must pay their dowries. There is no harm if you reach an understanding among yourselves about the dowry, God is all-knowing and all-wise."   

- Asserts male authority and maintenance over wives, and prescribes a three-step escalation for defiant wives: verbal admonishment, abandonment in bed, and physical striking.

4:34: "Men are in charge of women by [right of] what Allah has given one over the other and what they spend [for maintenance] from their wealth. So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in [the husband's] absence what Allah would have them guard. But those [wives] from whom you fear arrogance - [first] advise them; [then if they persist], forsake them in bed; and [finally], beat them. But if they obey you [once more], seek no means against them. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand."   

- States that disbelievers will be driven into hellfire, where their burned skins will be perpetually replaced with fresh skin to prolong their punishment.

4:56: "Indeed, those who disbelieve in our verses - We will drive them into a fire. Every time their skins are roasted through We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might and Wise."   

- Warns against allying with disbelievers who wish for Muslims to apostatize, commanding believers to capture and kill any who turn back or refuse to emigrate.

4:89: "They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate for the cause of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them and take not from among them any ally or helper."   

- Grants explicit authorization to seize and execute duplicitous individuals who refuse to offer peace or withhold hostility from the believers.

4:91: "You will find others who wish to obtain security from you and [to] obtain security from their people. Every time they are returned to [the influence of] disbelief, they fall back into it. So if they do not withdraw from you or offer you peace or restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you overtake them. And those - We have made for you against them a clear authorization"   

- Prescribes execution, crucifixion, amputation of alternating hands and feet, or exile for those who wage war against Allah and His messenger and spread corruption.

5:33: “This is the recompense of those who fight against Allah and His Messenger, and hasten about the earth, to do corruption there: they shall be slaughtered, or crucified, or their hands and feet shall alternately be struck off; or they shall be banished from the land. That is a degradation for them in this world; and in the world to come awaits them a mighty chastisement.”   

- Forbids taking Jews and Christians as allies, warning that any believer who forms such an alliance is regarded as one of them.

5:51: "O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you – then indeed, he is [one] of them. Indeed, Allah guides not the wrongdoing people."   

- Asserts that many jinn and humans were created specifically for Hell, describing them as spiritually obtuse, uncomprehending, and worse than livestock.

7:179: "And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. It is they who are the heedless."

- Instructs angelic forces to strike fear into unbelievers and physically strike their necks and fingertips during battle.

8:12: “When thy Lord was revealing to the angels, ‘I am with you; so confirm the believers. I shall cast into the unbelievers’ hearts terror; so smite above the necks, and smite every finger of them!”

- Directs warfare against opponents until all fitnah (persecution/strife) is eliminated and religious obedience belongs solely to Allah.

8:39: "And fight them until there is no fitnah and [until] the religion, all of it, is for Allah. And if they cease - then indeed, Allah is Seeing of what they do."

- Describes angels striking the faces and backs of disbelievers at the moment of death, consigning them to hellfire.

8:50: "And if you could but see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved... They are striking their faces and their backs and [saying], "Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire."

- Orders the hunting, capture, besieging, and killing of polytheists after sacred months expire, unless they convert, pray, and pay alms.

9:5: “Then, when the sacred months are drawn away, slay the idolaters wherever you find them, and take them, and confine them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they repent, and perform the prayer, and pay the alms, then let them go their way; Allah is All-forgiving, All-compassionate.”

- Declares polytheists ritually impure and permanently bars them from entering the Sacred Mosque in Mecca.

9:28: "O you who have believed, indeed the polytheists [non-Muslims] are unclean, so let them not approach al-Masjid al-haram after this, their [final] year. And if you fear privation, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise."

- Directs armed warfare against Jews and Christians who do not accept Islamic law until they pay tribute (jizya) in a state of submission.

9:29: “Fight those who believe not in Allah and the Last Day and do not forbid what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden — such men as practice not the religion of truth, being of those who have been given the Book — until they pay the tribute out of hand and have been humbled.”

- Commands the Prophet to wage harsh combat against disbelievers and hypocrites, warning them of destination in Hell.

9:73: "O Prophet, fight against the disbelievers and the hypocrites and be harsh upon them. And their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination"

- Asserts that Allah has traded Paradise to believers in exchange for their lives and property spent fighting, killing, and being killed in His cause.

9:111: “Allah has bought from the believers their selves and their possessions against the gift of Paradise; they fight in the way of Allah; they kill, and are killed; that is a promise binding upon Allah in the Torah, and the Gospel, and the Koran; and who fulfils his covenant truer than Allah? So rejoice in the bargain you have made with Him; that is the mighty triumph.”   

- Commands believers to fight adjacent unbelievers with visible harshness.

9:123: “O believers, fight the unbelievers who are near to you; and let them find in you a harshness; and know that Allah is with the godfearing.”

- Details graphic punishments in the afterlife for disbelievers, including garments of fire, boiling liquids melting their flesh and organs, and iron hooked rods to push them back into torment.

22:19-22: "These twain (the believers and the disbelievers) are two opponents who contend concerning their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, garments of fire will be cut out for them; boiling fluid will be poured down on their heads, Whereby that which is in their bellies, and their skins too, will be melted; And for them are hooked rods of iron. Whenever, in their anguish, they would go forth from thence they are driven back therein and (it is said unto them): Taste the doom of burning."   

- Instructs fighters to decapitate enemies in battle and take captives only after extensive slaughter, while promising divine reward to those slain in battle.

47:4: “When you meet the unbelievers, smite their necks, then, when you have made wide slaughter among them, tie fast the bonds; then set them free, either by grace or ransom, till the war lays down its loads. So it shall be; and if Allah had willed, He would have avenged Himself upon them; but that He may try some of you by means of others. And those who are slain in the way of Allah, He will not send their works astray.”   

- Describes Muhammad's followers as unyielding and fierce toward non-believers, but compassionate and gentle toward one another.

48:29: "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah ; and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves..."

- Forbids seeking peace treaties when holding military superiority over the adversary.

47:35: "So do not weaken and call for peace while you are superior; and Allah is with you and will never deprive you of [the reward of] your deeds."

- Recounts the expulsion of the Jewish tribe of Banu Nadir, attributing their defeat to divine terror cast into their hearts that caused the destruction of their homes.

59:2: "It is He who expelled the ones who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah ; but [the decree of] Allah came upon them from where they had not expected, and He cast terror into their hearts [so] they destroyed their houses by their [own] hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of vision."   

- Declares polytheists and disbelieving People of the Book to be the worst of creation, doomed to eternal damnation in Hell.

98:6: "Indeed, they who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. Those are the worst of creatures."

text:
📜🇺🇸 October 19, 1781: The British Surrender at Yorktown

After a three-week siege by about 17,000 American and French troops under George Washington and the Comte de Rochambeau, Lord Cornwallis surrendered his army of some 8,000 men at Yorktown, Virginia. A French fleet under Admiral de Grasse held the Chesapeake Bay, cutting off any escape by sea.

Cornwallis signed the Articles of Capitulation that day but stayed away from the ceremony, citing illness. Gen. Charles O'Hara offered his sword in his place, first to Rochambeau and then to Washington, who pointed him to Gen. Lincoln.

Yorktown ended major fighting in the Revolution and led to the Treaty of Paris in 1783.

Pictured: John Trumbull's painting in the U.S. Capitol Rotunda, with Gen. Benjamin Lincoln on the white horse accepting the British surrender.

text:
🚨 Every time I watch Arsenal I can't help but think about how perfect Morgan Rogers would be in the #10.

For example, below, Raya catches it, he rolls quickly to Rice so Arsenal can hurt Forest in transition, Rice looks up but Ødegaard is in front of the opposition's midfield line as opposed to behind it, Arsenal are forced to play slowly, and Forest recover into their defensive block with 11 men behind the ball.

Arsenal do get into their desired 3-1-3-3 / 3-1-6 eventually, but they lack transitional qualities to play through the pitch quickly.

Partly because none of the front 3 are especially devastating in transition (although Madueke on the left might have something to say about that), but also because they lack support from the #10 who is an #8 in reality.

If Arsenal had Rogers in the #10, he would be high and between the lines, receive on the back foot, turn and drive into space, and use his power (whether that be through carrying or passing + off-ball running) to make the team a MUCH bigger threat in these types of moments.

It's hard to break down a low block, and sometimes the best way to do it is not through directly breaking it down, but through exploiting them in the natural transitional moments that occur in games irrespective of the opposition's intentions to defend low.

Even when you play a low block there are countless opportunities to exploit the opponent in transition:

- when they lose possession,
- when you lose possession and counter-press,
- when they build and you press,
- when they go direct and you win 2nd balls,
- counter-attacking from their set-pieces,
- etc.

Jürgen Klopp's Liverpool were the masters at this because they could kill you in any moment, even if you didn't let them press reliably and killed their space by defending low. Football is a transitional game, and you cannot escape that no matter how you decide to play.

Besides, even though Ødegaard is a player who offers Arsenal incredible control and is an elite #8, games against teams like Forest don't suit him because the opposition don't build and they don't press. Ødegaard's primary use at Arsenal is to give the team control - when the opponent effectively gives it to you, his use evaporates because Arsenal no longer need him to drop deep to provide control with the ball or to lead the press.

Plus, when Arsenal are trying to break these teams down with close to 100 attacks per game, of course there will be moments when such a talented player influences the game positively with a delicate combination or a strong shot, for example, but the return for the volume of attacks is beyond average.

Arsenal would be far better off with Eze, Saka, Havertz, Merino, Dowman, or Guimarães in the #10 rather than Ødegaard in games like this, otherwise they lack a true #10 type profile in the midfield.

The Rice-Bruno Guimarães-Ødegaard midfield 3 also suffers because, on paper, the balance is Rice #6, Bruno G #8, Ødegaard #10, but they are not collectively reliably occupying spaces high.

With how Arsenal play both of their fullbacks consistently on the top line, it's not the job of the #6 or the #8 to reliably join the attack, so the onus is MASSIVELY on the #10 to stay away positionally and to be the driving creative force from midfield, but Ødegaard is not the right profile for this in every regard - positionally, athletically to carry or run beyond + overlap/underlap, and even technically because he is one-footed and lacks power to play transitional passes or to whip unstoppable crosses into the box.

Ødegaard would be better in a David Silva-esque role as the left #10 because that would force him to be more direct with less favourable angles to cut inside, but Arsenal's dynamics aren't set up that way. The #10 is either right-sided or central. Not on the left.

People waxed lyrical about his performance against Napoli but it took Arsenal about 100 attacks for him to do anything. Is that return good enough? No. It’s not. You need to have a much better return than that, whether that be goal threat or assist threat. At least 10 PL #10’s have a bigger threat than him here. As do 6 Arsenal players, most of which are not even #10’s.

People talk about the attack, but Ødegaard is part of it, and he is not good enough in the #10 for Arsenal. It is obvious in games against Forest when Arsenal have 100 attacks vs a low block or in games when Arsenal have much less of the ball and need a proper #10 to get them up the pitch (see PSG in the Champions League final).

text:
When is a large language model a good calibration agent? Physics-labeled prompting for budgeted engineering simulator calibration : https://t.co/hUyfyNU90I

"Ruo-Qian Wangrq.wang@rutgers.edu organization=Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Rutgers University, addressline=500 Bartholomew Rd, city=Piscataway, state=NJ, postcode=08854, country=USA
Abstract
Calibrating an expensive engineering simulator means selecting uncertain model parameters so that simulated outputs match reference data, and the cost of doing so is dominated by the number of simulator runs the outer loop consumes. This paper asks whether a large language model (LLM), given a plain-text description of what is physically wrong with the current run, can select those runs more efficiently than a conventional derivative-free optimizer. The test cases are a large-eddy simulation of flow past a circular cylinder, calibrated against force-coefficient statistics, and an inexpensive damped-oscillator inverse problem. The physics-labeled prompt is compared with four ablated prompts, in which the diagnostic text is removed, anonymized, replaced by length-matched filler, or deliberately misdirected, and with Nelder–Mead, Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization, covariance-matrix adaptation and random search. All methods start from the same initial design. Because a language model returns a different answer each time it is called, the physics-labeled prompt is repeated 25 times and the ablated prompts 30 times, so that the comparison can be tested rather than merely described. The physical description produces a clear advantage over the ablated prompts during the first few simulator runs. Its first informed proposal improved on the best point of the shared starting design in 23 of 25 repeats, against 8 of 30 for the ablated prompts. In objective terms the median calibration error after five runs is 21.9 times lower than with the physics removed, 4.7 times lower after ten runs, and indistinguishable after fifteen. The repeats also quantify how variable the model itself is: identical prompts and identical starting points return five-seed medians spanning a factor of 9.8, which exceeds many of the effects this literature reports from five runs alone. Because the advantage does not persist, the LLM is used as a warm start and the accumulated runs are handed to a conventional optimizer at a fixed budget. The resulting workflow reaches the target accuracy in 9 simulator runs, against 12 for the LLM alone, 11–14 for the ablated prompts, 17 for Nelder–Mead and more than 60 for Bayesian optimization or random search. The eight runs saved relative to Nelder–Mead amount to roughly half an hour of solver time in the present case and to most of a working day on a simulator with hour-scale evaluations. A sensitivity analysis over all 3 047 solver evaluations shows that the chosen force statistics constrain only one of the three calibrated parameters, which bounds how far any such ranking can be pushed. Physical descriptions buy an early sense of direction; they do not buy convergence.

1Introduction
Engineering simulators encode decades of domain knowledge, but their practical value usually depends on calibration: selecting uncertain parameters so that simulated outputs match reference data. The cost of calibration is dominated by the outer loop that decides which simulation to run next. When one evaluation costs hours of solver time, the available budget may permit only a handful of decisions, and the quality of the first few determines whether a usable calibration is reached before the budget is exhausted. Calibration performance is therefore governed by more than final parameter accuracy. The number of evaluations spent sets the computational cost, and the quality of the early decisions sets how efficiently that cost is incurred.Two strategies have dominated practice, and they draw on different information (Fig. 1). The first is conventional derivative-free optimization. Nelder–Mead, covariance-matrix adaptation and Bayesian optimization (Conn et al., 2009; Nelder and Mead, 1965; Hansen et al., 2003; Snoek et al., 2012) are general and automatic, but they treat parameters as anonymous coordinates and infer search directions from the numerical history alone. The second is expert judgment. Human engineers inspect interpretable discrepancies, such as an overly damped oscillator, suppressed vortex shedding, an incorrect drag level or a shifted phase, and translate these into directed parameter changes. The expert loop uses information that the numerical methods discard, but it is labor-intensive, subjective and hard to reproduce, because the reasoning behind each adjustment is rarely written down (Wang et al., 2011). Neither strategy serves the whole budget well. Model-based optimizers can learn useful relationships between parameters and objective values, but only once enough evaluations have accumulated to build a reliable approximation of the response, which leaves a gap in exactly the early regime where a directed guess would be most valuable. Expert judgment fills that gap, but it is itself uncertain and it scales poorly as the number of calibrated parameters grows.Large language models (LLMs) offer one route to closing that gap. An LLM conditions on natural language and can act as an iterative proposal engine, generating candidate solutions from a record of previous attempts (Yang et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2024; Nie et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2024). Two questions follow for engineering practice. The first is whether an LLM can serve as a calibration agent that consumes physically interpretable diagnostics and proposes the next simulator evaluation well enough to justify its place in the loop under a tight budget. The second is whether the physics competence that LLMs display when answering questions converts into useful action. Calibration is a stronger test than question answering, because the model must turn a description of a physical discrepancy into a specific intervention and is scored on whether the simulator output actually improves. Testing this requires a controlled comparison rather than a demonstration. The diagnostic language can be removed, anonymized, length-matched or deliberately misdirected while the numerical history is held fixed, which isolates the contribution of the physical content.Because the use of LLMs for optimization and calibration is new to the engineering literature, the mechanism is stated here before the experiments. At each iteration the model receives a plain-text record of the parameter vectors already evaluated together with their objective values and, in the physics-labeled case, a few sentences naming which physical quantities are off and in which direction: that the wake is shedding too slowly, or that the lift amplitude is too weak. It returns one parameter vector in machine-readable form, which is clipped to the bounds and passed to the simulator (Fig. 1). No training, fitting or differentiation takes place. No surrogate response surface is built and no weights are updated, and the entire adaptation occurs inside a single prompt. The contrast with model-based optimization is instructive. Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization also proposes points from an evaluation history, but it does so by fitting an explicit probabilistic surrogate and maximizing an acquisition function over it, and that surrogate becomes informative only as evaluations accumulate. The LLM builds no such object. What it brings instead is whatever prior association it carries between a described physical symptom and a plausible parameter change. It also carries none of the guarantees of a numerical method: a language model can emit unparseable output, propose infeasible points or repeat a point it has already evaluated, and it has no convergence property.📷Figure 1:Three strategies for engineering simulator calibration under a limited evaluation budget: conventional numerical optimization, expert-guided calibration based on physical discrepancies, and a physics-labeled LLM proposal policy. The proposed workflow combines optimization history with physically interpretable diagnostics to select the next bounded simulator evaluation, and hands the accumulated evaluations to a numerical optimizer once the semantic channel is exhausted.
This study therefore asks whether an LLM supplied with physical background information can be built into a more efficient calibration agent. The main contributions are as follows.
1.A bounded, physics-labeled LLM proposal policy is formulated for budgeted engineering simulator calibration and paired with a numerical continuation step that transfers the accumulated evaluations to Nelder–Mead or Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization (GP-BO) at a fixed handoff budget.
2.The early advantage of the physical description is established by repeating each prompt many times rather than by comparing single trajectories. The clearest readout is the outcome of the first informed proposal, which improved on the shared starting design in 23 of 25 repeats of the physics-labeled prompt against 8 of 30 for the ablated prompts. In objective terms, the median best objective is 21.9 times lower at five evaluations and 4.7 times lower at ten evaluations, and the two are indistinguishable at fifteen.
3.The run-to-run variability of the LLM proposal policy is measured at fixed seed. Five arms running an identical policy on identical starting designs return five-seed medians spanning a factor of 9.8 at five evaluations. This sets a resolution floor that any five-seed LLM-optimizer comparison must clear, and to our knowledge it has not previously been quantified on an engineering simulator.
4.The continuation step converts the transient advantage into a usable procedure. It matches the LLM early and Nelder–Mead late, and reaches an objective of 10−4 in a median of 9 evaluations against 12 for the pure LLM policy, 11–14 for the ablated prompts and 17 for Nelder–Mead.
5.A sensitivity analysis of the benchmark over all 3 047 solver evaluations shows that only the molecular viscosity is identifiable from the four target statistics. This bounds which parts of the reported trajectories carry information and which sit inside the noise floor, and such a screen is recommended as routine practice before ranking optimizers on a calibration benchmark.
2Related work

2.1Engineering simulator calibration
Calibration of computer models is a classical inverse problem in engineering, geoscience and uncertainty quantification (Kennedy and O’Hagan, 2001; Sung and Tuo, 2024). When gradients are unavailable or unreliable, derivative-free optimization provides a general outer-loop strategy (Conn et al., 2009). Applications include climate-model parameter tuning (Tett et al., 2017), engineering analysis model validation (Wang et al., 2011) and ensemble-based calibration of complex numerical models (Dunbar et al., 2022). The advantage of these methods is their generality. Their limitation is that they usually operate on anonymous numerical coordinates and scalar objectives, discarding much of the interpretable physical information that engineers use when diagnosing a failed simulation.This paper adopts two conventions from that literature. The first is that comparisons of derivative-free methods are conventionally reported through budget-to-target statistics and data profiles rather than through a single terminal objective (Moré and Wild, 2009), because the quantity of practical interest is how many evaluations are needed to reach an acceptable accuracy. The second is that the identifiability of the calibrated parameters conditions any such comparison. If part of the parameter vector is weakly constrained by the chosen observables, the corresponding portion of the objective landscape is flat and optimizer rankings within it are not informative (Kennedy and O’Hagan, 2001).
2.2LLMs as proposal mechanisms
Optimization by prompting treats an LLM as an iterative proposal engine that receives a history of attempted solutions and returns a new candidate (Yang et al., 2024). Related work uses LLMs to guide evolutionary search or to exploit directional feedback (Liu et al., 2024; Nie et al., 2024). Recent studies also point to limitations: performance may depend on model size, prompt template, task distribution, and whether the feedback contains actionable directions (Zhang et al., 2024). For engineering applications this motivates careful benchmarking against derivative-free methods and prompt ablations, rather than broad claims that an LLM is itself a superior https://t.co/wIEGaMNw6G issue is largely absent from this literature, namely the variability of the proposals themselves. Trajectories on an expensive simulator are typically reported over a handful of seeds, and the seed is usually assumed to control the whole experiment, which it does not. A stochastic decoder returns different proposals on repeated calls with an identical prompt, so the seed fixes the initial design and the numerical baselines but leaves the language model free to vary. An LLM policy is therefore a distribution over trajectories even when the environment is fully seeded, and a curve obtained from a single arm confounds policy quality with decoder sampling. The number of repeats required to resolve a given effect follows from the width of that distribution. This width is measured directly here and used to judge how much of the observed benchmark separation can be trusted.
2.3LES calibration as an engineering test case
The main engineering case in this paper is calibration of a Smagorinsky-type LES closure (Smagorinsky, 1963; Lilly, 1967) for flow past a circular cylinder, a canonical vortex-shedding problem (Williamson, 1996). The simulator is run through OpenFOAM (Weller et al., 1998); the outer loop varies closure and viscosity parameters and compares force-coefficient statistics against reference data. This setting suits the present question because the simulator output contains meaningful diagnostics while each evaluation is costly enough that early-budget behavior matters. As Section 5.5 shows, it is also a setting in which the observables constrain the closure coefficients only weakly. That behavior is typical of force-statistics-based calibration, and it is the reason the sensitivity analysis is reported alongside the optimizer comparison.
3Physics-labeled LLM calibration with numerical continuation

3.1Calibration problem
Let x∈𝒳 denote bounded simulator parameters, S⁡(x) the simulator output, and y⋆ the target observation or reference output. The calibration objective isminx∈𝒳⁡J⁡(x),(1)where J is available only by running the simulator and post-processing its output. In addition to J⁡(x), the evaluator may return a diagnostic vector d⁡(x) and a short text summary q⁡(x) describing the physical discrepancy. The prompt-based proposal policy receives a historyℋt={xi,J⁡(xi),d⁡(xi),q⁡(xi)}i=1t(2)and returns a new bounded candidate xt+1.The physics-labeled LLM policy used here is deliberately simple. The prompt lists the parameter bounds, the ten best previous trials sorted by objective, and a concise physical diagnostic block for the incumbent. The model is required to return a machine-readable parameter vector, and invalid or out-of-bounds proposals are clipped or retried by the driver script. The full physics-labeled policy is referred to as Phys-OPRO where a short name is convenient, although the paper emphasizes the workflow rather than the method name. The complete prompt text is reproduced in Appendix A, and the parsing and retry logic are given in Appendix C.
3.2Numerical continuation
An advantage confined to the first few evaluations is of limited use unless the workflow specifies when to stop relying on it. If physical semantics help only while the numerical history is uninformative, the deliverable is a warm-start rule rather than a stand-alone optimizer. The policy described above is treated accordingly. Once the numerical history is informative, an LLM has no mechanism for local refinement and, as Section 5.6 shows, spends an increasing share of its budget re-proposing points it has already evaluated.A two-stage policy is therefore defined. This property is used in Sections 5.1 and 5.2.
3.3Prompt controls
To separate physical semantics from generic prompt effects, several controls are evaluated (Table 1). The no-diagnostic prompt removes the physical diagnostic text and leaves only the parameter and objective history. The anonymized prompt retains the numeric metric values but replaces parameter and metric names by anonymous symbols. The length-matched prompt replaces the diagnostic language with inert filler text of comparable length while retaining the numeric values. The evaluation keeps three comparisons separate. text:
Some women survive. Some women endure. Elizabeth Morrow built a future out of loss, hard work, and a baby on her back. And she called it love.

She buried her husband, gave birth two days later, and returned to work before the week was over.
It was 1887 in Dodge City, Kansas, and Elizabeth Morrow was only twenty two when everything she thought her life would be collapsed in a matter of days.
Her husband caught typhoid without warning. One moment he was standing in their small rented room, promising that things would get better. Three days later, he was gone. Fever stole his voice. Delirium stole his recognition. Death came quickly and without mercy. There was no goodbye, no last conversation, no time to prepare for what came next.
Elizabeth stood beside his grave alone. She was pregnant, penniless, and already in debt for the funeral. Every coin used to bury him was borrowed. Every face around her belonged to someone who could offer sympathy but not survival. Grief pressed down on her chest, but she did not have the luxury of falling apart. There was no one else to carry what was coming.

Two days later, her daughter was born.

The child arrived screaming, furious, alive. A small miracle wrapped in exhaustion and fear. Elizabeth held her with shaking arms and understood immediately that her life no longer belonged to her alone. She had no family to fall back on. No inheritance. No safety net. The world she lived in did not forgive widows, and it certainly did not protect young women with babies and empty pockets.

So she worked.

She washed other people’s clothes until her fingers cracked and bled. She scrubbed whiskey off saloon floors before sunrise. She hauled water, cleaned rooms, and washed sheets at a hotel late into the night while her newborn slept in a neighbor’s spare room two blocks away. She counted hours instead of days. Pennies instead of dreams.
Some nights she ate almost nothing. Some mornings her body felt too heavy to lift. But rent was always paid. Her daughter was always fed. And no matter how raw her throat felt, she sang lullabies every night, refusing to let the child hear the tears she swallowed.

Time moved slowly, but it moved forward.

Years passed. The baby grew. Elizabeth never asked for help. She never stopped pushing. In 1895, she saved just enough to open a tiny boarding house. Four rooms. One stove. No room for mistakes. It was not comfort, but it was hers. In those walls lived everything she had fought for.

By 1900, she owned the building outright.

Her daughter Mary watched her mother’s hands harden and split from years of labor. She watched her bend, but never break. She learned early what strength actually looked like. Not loud. Not celebrated. Just steady and relentless. Stories like this are why Evolvarium exists, because quiet lives often carry the loudest truths. 

In 1923, Mary stood on a stage at Dodge City High to give her commencement speech. She did not talk about herself. She talked about her mother.

She told the crowd that dignity is not something handed to you. It is something you decide not to give up.
Elizabeth sat among the audience, older now, her body marked by decades of work. She had never been famous. Her name would never appear in history books. But she had lived long enough to see her daughter succeed, to hold her grandchildren, and to know that hunger and fear would end with her.

Years later, someone asked her how she survived it all.

She thought quietly before answering.

Every morning, she looked at her child and made herself a promise. That her daughter would never know hunger. That she would never have to beg. And that promise was stronger than grief, stronger than exhaustion, stronger than fear.

Some women survive.
Some women endure.

Elizabeth Morrow built a future out of loss, hard work, and a baby on her back. And she called it love.

The Myth of Parallel Priesthoods: A Textual Examination of Hebrews 7–10
A recurring proposition within certain theological circles asserts that the Aaronic (Levitical) priesthood remains fully active, legally binding, and eternally distinct on earth, operating alongside a separate, purely celestial High Priesthood held by Jesus Christ. Under this construct, Christ’s Melchizedekian priesthood is treated not as a replacement or transfer of the earthly order, but merely as a non-intersecting, parallel administration in heaven.

This model collapses when subjected to the forensic, grammatical, and theological arguments recorded in the Epistle to the Hebrews. The canonical author does not argue for dual, co-equal jurisdictions running simultaneously. The inspired argument demonstrates that the earthly Levitical apparatus was a temporary, typological shadow, explicitly altered, annulled, and superseded by the entrance of the Melchizedekian High Priest.

1. The Fallacy of the Earthly Exemption: Misinterpreting Hebrews 8:4
The bedrock text often cited to defend parallel jurisdictions is Hebrews 8:4:

"For if he were on earth, he should not be a priest, seeing that there are priests that offer gifts according to the law."

Advocates of the parallel model claim this verse proves Christ was barred from the earthly priesthood by divine design, leaving the earthly Aaronic system untouched and perpetual.

This reading wrenches the clause out of its immediate syntax. The author is using a present counterfactual (unreal condition) in the Greek: “If He were on earth [which He is not], He would not even be a priest [under that earthly jurisdiction], since there are already those offering the gifts according to the Law.”

The point is not to protect the autonomy of the Levitical altar, but to demonstrate its ontological inferiority:

Verse 5 immediately qualifies the earthly priests: They serve what is merely a copy (ὑπόδειγμα, hypodeigma) and a shadow (σκιά, skia) of the heavenly sanctuary.

Verse 6 establishes the contrast: Christ’s ministry is superior precisely because it mediates a covenant enacted on better promises, rendering the shadow obsolete.

The author does not say, “Therefore, the earthly altar continues indefinitely alongside Him.” Rather, the existence of earthly priests was tied strictly to the earthly copy. Once the substance arrived and entered the genuine, uncreated sanctuary (Heb 9:11–12), the function of the shadow was judicially fulfilled.

2. Lexical Proofs of Covenantal Transformation
The Greek text of Hebrews employs precise legal and forensic terminology to define what occurred between the Levitical order and the Melchizedekian priesthood.

A. The Verdict of Incompletion and the Transfer of the Priesthood (Hebrews 7:11–12)
The legal necessity of the transition begins with the author’s foundational challenge in Hebrews 7:11:

Εἰ μὲν οὖν τελείωσις διὰ τῆς Λευιτικῆς ἱερωσύνης ἦν, (ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς νενομοθέτηται,) τίς ἔτι χρεία κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδὲκ ἕτερον ἀνίστασθαι ἱερέα καὶ οὐ κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Ἀαρὼν λέγεσθαι;"If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?"

If the Levitical system had the structural capacity to accomplish perfection (τελείωσις, teleiōsis), the introduction of another priesthood would be entirely superfluous. The author then immediately delivers the judicial consequence in Hebrews 7:12:

μετατιθεμένης γὰρ τῆς ἱερωσύνης ἐξ ἀνάγκης καὶ νόμου μετάθεσις γίνεται."For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law."

The term used is μετατίθημι (metatithēmi), appearing here as the present passive participle μετατιθεμένης (metatithemenēs), followed by the noun μετάθεσις (metathesis):

In classical and biblical Greek, metatithēmi denotes a transfer, transformation, transposition, or removal.

The author uses the identical verb in Hebrews 11:5 to describe the removal of Enoch: "Enoch was translated/taken up (μετετέθη) that he should not see death."

Enoch was not duplicated to live in two dimensions at once; he was relocated. Likewise, the priesthood was not duplicated into parallel earthly and heavenly tracks; its authority and administrative basis were fundamentally altered and transferred.

Because the priesthood and the Law were bound together—the law was codified under the Levitical priesthood (Heb 7:11)—altering the priesthood legally required an unavoidable alteration (μετάθεσις) of the Law itself.

B. The Irrevocable Divine Oath (Hebrews 7:20–22)

Καὶ καθ’ ὅσον οὐ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας, (οἱ μὲν γὰρ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας εἰσὶν ἱερεῖς γεγονότες, ὁ δὲ μετὰ ὁρκωμοσίας διὰ τοῦ λέγοντος πρὸς αὐτόν, Ὤμοσεν Κύριος καὶ οὐ μεταμεληθήσεται, Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισεδέκ·) κατὰ τοσοῦτο κρείττονος διαθήκης γέγονεν ἔγγυος Ἰησοῦς."And inasmuch as not without an oath he was made priest: (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:) By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament."

The forensic foundation of this transfer is grounded in the presence versus absence of an ὁρκωμοσία (horkōmosia—sworn oath):
The Aaronic priests were installed χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας (chōris horkōmosias, without an oath, v. 21). Their tenure was established purely under a provisional statute (νόμος ἐντολῆς σαρκίνης, "law of a carnal commandment," v. 16), inherently subject to administrative revision, suspension, and expiration.

In absolute contrast, the Melchizedekian High Priest was instituted through the unalterable oath of God invoking Psalm 110:4: "The Lord sware and will not repent (οὐ μεταμεληθήσεται)."

God bound Himself by His own nature to guarantee the perpetuity of this singular High Priest. Because the Aaronic order lacked an immutable divine oath guaranteeing its perpetuity, it possessed no legal framework to maintain permanent or parallel status once the sworn Priest of Psalm 110:4 took His seat. Jesus thus stands as the sole ἔγγυος (engyos—legal guarantor/surety) of an entirely superior covenant (v. 22).

C. The Formal Revocation of the Prior Mandate (Hebrews 7:18)

ἀθέτησις μὲν γὰρ γίνεται προαγούσης ἐντολῆς διὰ τὸ αὐτῆς ἀσθενὲς καὶ ἀνωφελές."For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof."

The author selects the noun ἀθέτησις (athetēsis):

In ancient Hellenistic jurisprudence and papyrological records, athetēsis was the formal technical term for the legal cancellation, annulment, or revocation of a decree, contract, or treaty.
It means to render something invalid or devoid of legal force.

What was formally cancelled? The προαγούσης ἐντολῆς (proagousēs entolēs)—the preceding commandment concerning the carnal lineage and sacrificial administration of the Levitical system (Heb 7:16). The commandment was not placed on reserve; it was set aside because it could never bring perfection (τελείωσις, teleiōsis, v. 19).

D. The Abolition of the First to Establish the Second (Hebrews 10:9)

ἀναιρεῖ τὸ πρῶτον ἵνα τὸ δεύτερον στήσῃ."He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second."

The verb ἀναιρέω (anaireō) carries the explicit meaning to take away, abolish, or terminate:

The Greek syntax sets up an absolute mutual exclusivity: τὸ πρῶτον (the first order of animal sacrifices and Levitical offerings, vv. 5–8) is definitively taken away so that τὸ δεύτερον (the will of God fulfilled in the singular, once-for-all body of Christ, v. 10) may be legally established (στήσῃ).

One cannot "establish the second" while insisting the "first" remains permanently operational. One yields to the other.
3. The Temporal Nature of the Earthly Apparatus

The Epistle to the Hebrews systematically bars any interpretation that grants eternal continuity to the earthly cultus through its precise, forensic Greek vocabulary:

In Hebrews 9:9, the author identifies the outer tabernacle and its ritual system as merely a παραβολή (parabolē)—a temporal figure, symbol, or parable for the present age that was fundamentally incapable of perfecting or cleansing the worshiper’s conscience.

Furthermore, Hebrews 9:10 establishes an explicit expiration date on these dietary regulations and external, carnal ordinances, stating they were legally imposed only μέχρι καιροῦ διορθώσεως (mechri kairou diorthōseōs)—strictly until the designated time of reformation, rectification, and setting things right, a threshold brought to fulfillment in Christ.

This terminal design is reinforced in Hebrews 8:13, where the declaration of a "New Covenant" carries immediate judicial consequences: by using the perfect verb πεπαλαίωκεν (pepalaiōken), God formally pronounced the first covenant antiquated and obsolete. The author immediately adds that whatever is obsolete and growing old stands ἐγγὺς ἀφανισμοῦ (engys aphanismou)—on the precipice of vanishing and total disappearance.

Finally, the definitive end of the repetitive Levitical cycle is sealed in Hebrews 9:12 and 10:10 with the absolute adverbs ἅπαξ (hapax) and ἐφάπαξ (ephapax). Christ entered the heavenly holy place once for all, securing an eternal redemption that permanently dismantled and terminated any ongoing theological necessity for daily, repeating animal sacrifices.
4. The Canonical Inadmissibility of Future/Parallel Levitical Atonement (The Ezekiel 40–48 Objection)

A common theological refuge for the parallel model is an appeal to the visionary temple of Ezekiel 40–48, asserting that an earthly, Zadokite-Levitical priesthood must offer blood sacrifices in an earthly sanctuary alongside Christ.

Subjected to the canonical hierarchy of Scripture, this premise fails:

Explicit Text Over Visionary Symbolism: A sound Berean hermeneutic requires interpreting Old Covenant apocalyptic and visionary literature through the clear, didactic doctrinal revelation of the New Testament, not the reverse. Ezekiel received a vision framed in the typological vocabulary and ceremonial categories of his day to communicate the holiness, pure worship, and unmediated dwelling of God with His people.

The Theological Impossibility of Expiation: Ezekiel 45:15–20 explicitly states that those visionary offerings were designed "to make reconciliation for them" and "for an atonement." To claim this operates literally under a continuing or re-instituted Aaronic administration creates an irreconcilable contradiction with Hebrews 10:1–4, which declares that the blood of bulls and goats could never take away sins.

The Fallacy of "Memorial" Offerings: Proponents frequently attempt to bypass Hebrews 10:18 by asserting that Ezekiel's visionary sacrifices are merely retrospective "memorials" (analogous to the bread and cup of the New Covenant). The Hebrew text utterly refutes this claim: Ezekiel repeatedly uses the covenantal terms לְכַפֵּר (l'khapper — "to make atonement / expiate," Ezek 45:15, 17, 20) and חַטָּאת (chattath — "sin offering," Ezek 43:19). The text nowhere employs the statutory term for a memorial (זִכָּרוֹן, zikkaron). To attribute expiatory language to a future animal altar after Christ has secured eternal redemption (Heb 9:12) is to declare the blood of the covenant an unholy or insufficient thing (Heb 10:29).
The Finality of Absolute Forgiveness: To argue that God ordains a parallel earthly sacrificial altar—whether contemporary with the apostolic era or in an earthly millennial construct—collides directly with the forensic ceiling established in Hebrews 10:18:
"Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin."If remission (ἄφεσις, aphesis—total legal release and pardon) has been secured by the Melchizedekian High Priest, the canonical author states flatly that an offering for sin no longer exists (οὐκέτι προσφορά). Elevating an earthly priesthood to continue offering blood for sin reduces the cross of Christ to a provisional act and directly violates apostolic doctrine.

The Theological Reality

To claim that the Levitical priesthood continues unchanged alongside the Melchizedekian priesthood is to reconstruct the very wall of separation that the cross tore down:

Sacrificial Redundancy: If the Aaronic priesthood retains legitimate, God-ordained authority to offer animal blood on earth for atonement, the once-for-all sacrifice of Christ is reduced to an incomplete act. Hebrews 10:18 establishes the definitive rule: “Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.”

One Altar, Not Two: The apostolic text explicitly bars the old order from partaking of the new: “We have an altar, whereof they have no right to eat which serve the tabernacle” (Heb 13:10). The text establishes that believers possess an altar from which those who serve the earthly tent have no legal standing or right to eat. The two systems do not share jurisdiction.

The Melchizedekian Ascendancy: Melchizedek was superior to Abraham because Abraham paid tithes to him, and Levi, being in the loins of Abraham, paid tithes through him (Heb 7:7–10). If the lesser paid homage to the greater in type, the lesser cannot maintain a competitive, independent administration against the antitype—the risen Lord.

The canonical verdict of the New Testament is unified: the shadow has yielded to the substance. The priesthood was transferred, the preliminary ordinance was legally annulled, and the first was taken away to establish the everlasting reign of the Great High Priest of the order of Melchizedek.

text:
"Not Basic Income, But High Income: The Abundance Paradox of the AI ​​and Robot Age"

In July 2026, at Tesla's Texas Gigafactory, Zani Minton Baders, editor-in-chief of *The Economist*, had a conversation with Elon Musk lasting over 90 minutes. Musk reiterated his long-held assertion: artificial intelligence and robots will jointly usher in an era of "amazing abundance." Not universal basic income, but universal high income.

This statement is significant because it's not just an optimistic response to unemployment, but a subversion of the entire definition of economics.

The essence of economics is rewritten.

Musk offers a concise, almost cold, definition: the economy is the production of goods and the provision of services. With enough robots, coupled with powerful digital intelligence, the economy approaches "quasi-infinite." Within this framework, the core constraint of traditional economics—scarcity—is loosened by machine productivity.

He further predicts that by 2036, "money will no longer matter." People will need money for food, housing, transportation, and entertainment. When robots and AI can provide goods and services far exceeding what any human can consume, the marginal utility of money drops dramatically. More importantly, he advocates for the Treasury to directly issue checks to citizens, asserting that this won't trigger inflation but could instead lead to deflation—because output growth would far outpace money supply growth.

This logic rests on the premise that AI and robots not only replace labor but also push the marginal cost of a large number of goods and services close to zero. Historical experience tells us that technology typically replaces specific jobs first, then creates new ones. This time, the difference lies in the speed and scope. Musk estimates that within about five years, AI could surpass the total intelligence of all humanity; within ten years, almost every job could be done better by machines.

The Gap Between "High" and "Basic" Universal basic income focuses on the minimum standard of survival. Universal high income points to a completely different standard: not just ensuring people barely survive, but enabling the majority to enjoy a quality of life that only a very few can afford today.

Musk has repeatedly emphasized this point on various occasions. He has even stated that when robots and superintelligence emerge, everyone in the world will have access to better healthcare than they have. This statement, though seemingly exaggerated, points to a profound shift: sectors traditionally heavily reliant on human capital, such as healthcare, housing, education, and entertainment, will experience a significant increase in supply elasticity once machines take over on a large scale.

He repeatedly cites Iain M. Banks' *Culture* series as a reference. In that setting, highly intelligent "minds" are responsible for production and coordination, and biological humans hardly need to work for survival, instead pursuing games, art, exploration, and interpersonal interaction. Musk doesn't entirely accept Banks' political philosophy (Banks himself has clear socialist leanings), but he endorses this materialistic vision of a post-scarcity society.

The difference lies in this: basic income is compensation for "job loss"; high income is the distribution of "productivity explosion." The former is defensive, the latter expansionary.

🌎 MARKET FORECAST — MONDAY, OCTOBER 19, 2026

📰 Overnight News Update

• 🇺🇸 Intel: JPMorgan upgraded $INTC from Underweight to Neutral with an $85 price target. Shares were up roughly 3.8% pre-market, providing a fresh semiconductor catalyst.

• 🇺🇸 Defense M&A: $RCAT announced a proposed €39-per-share cash acquisition of Steyr Motors, valued at approximately $230M. The transaction remains subject to approvals and closing conditions.

• 🇫🇷 Europe: Political unrest and fiscal concerns in France are weighing on sentiment, with European equities and the euro under pressure.

🎯 Pre-Market Bias: Cautiously Bullish

🌏 Overnight

• 🇨🇳 China Q3 GDP grew 4.5% vs 4.4% expected. September industrial production rose 5.5%, while retail sales increased just 1.1%, highlighting resilient exports but weak domestic demand.

• 🇰🇷 South Korea’s KOSPI rebounded roughly 1.8% after last week’s semiconductor rout. A reported Samsung/TSMC collaboration involving Nvidia’s next-generation HBM remains unconfirmed by the companies.

• 🇯🇵🇹🇼 Japan’s Nikkei and Taiwan’s TAIEX both slipped around 0.6%, showing that Asian semiconductor participation remains uneven.

🇺🇸 Today’s Catalysts

• Pre-market: Nasdaq fut +~1.1% | S&P fut +~0.5% | Dow slightly green — pointing to a semiconductor-led recovery attempt.

• US 10Y yield eased toward ~5.07–5.09%, providing some valuation relief for technology and AI names.

• DXY ~101.9 | BTC >$82K | Brent -~1.8%. Lower oil is supportive for inflation expectations, while Bitcoin is showing modest risk-on improvement.

• European equities remain weaker, with the STOXX 600 down ~0.7% and France’s CAC 40 off more than 1%.

• 10:00 ET — NAHB Housing Index: consensus 31 vs 32 prior.

• Earnings this week: Tesla, Meta, Lam Research and Texas Instruments — with AI spending, semiconductor demand and capex guidance in focus.

📈 Reaction Map

• Risk-on: 45%

• Choppy/mixed: 35%

• Risk-off: 20%

🔥 Possible Winners

• MU / MUU / MULL / SNDK / SNXX — potential memory-recovery candidates after aggressive liquidation, provided sector breadth continues improving.

• NVDA / AVGO / AMD / AMDL / SOXL — potential beneficiaries of lower yields and renewed semiconductor buying.

• INTC — fresh analyst upgrade provides a company-specific catalyst, though the pre-market move increases chase risk.

• TSM / ASML / AMAT / LRCX — advanced-chip investment remains supportive, with Lam Research earnings later this week an important sector read-through.

• AAOI / AAOX / LITE / LITX / COHR — potential rebound candidates if money rotates back into AI networking and optics.

• COIN / CONL / MSTR / MSTU — could benefit if Bitcoin maintains its recovery and broader risk appetite improves.

⚠️ Possible Losers / Risks

• MU / MULL / SNDK / SNXX — Chinese memory competition and last week’s severe institutional selling remain important sentiment risks.

• NVDA / AVGO / ORCL / ORCX / DELL / DLLL — AI-infrastructure financing costs and return-on-investment concerns remain unresolved.

• SOXL / AMDL / MVLL — highly vulnerable to another sharp reversal if the semiconductor rebound fades.

• SOXS becomes the tactical bearish vehicle if Nasdaq strength fails and semiconductor selling resumes.

💰 Profit-Taking Watch: Moderate

• Last week’s sharp semiconductor decline creates room for short-covering and a rebound, but concentrated AI positioning, weak European markets and unresolved financing concerns increase the risk of selling into strength.

🧭 Bottom Line

• Monday offers a credible semiconductor recovery attempt, supported by stronger U.S. futures, lower Treasury yields, softer oil and improving Korean sentiment.

🦃🇺🇸🇿🇦 INTRODUCING A THANKSGIVING ACROSS AMERICA!

The Tradition Continues. The Table Grows.

This Thanksgiving, The Bridge to Liberty is launching a special nationwide initiative to bring American families and newly arrived Afrikaner refugees together through one of America’s most cherished traditions: Thanksgiving.

For many of our Afrikaner friends, this will be their very first American Thanksgiving. They may be thousands of miles from the homeland they have always known, beginning new lives in unfamiliar communities without extended family or friends nearby.

We want to change that.

Through our American Neighbor Network, we hope to connect Afrikaner families with welcoming American families who would be willing to share their Thanksgiving table, extend a hand of friendship, and introduce them to this beautiful American tradition.

For families who cannot be connected with an American host, The Bridge to Liberty hopes to provide grocery gift cards to help them prepare their own traditional Thanksgiving dinner or purchase a prepared holiday meal.

❤️ OUR INITIAL GOAL IS 25 AFRIKANER FAMILIES ACROSS AMERICA!

But we don’t want to stop there! Depending on the response from participating families and the generosity of our donors, we may be able to expand this initiative to include even more families.

The more support we receive, the more Thanksgiving tables we can help fill!

⛪ We are also inviting American churches, families, and individuals across the country to participate in our American Neighbor Network, a year-round initiative dedicated to building friendships, fellowship, and community connections for newly arrived Afrikaner families.

🇿🇦❤️🇺🇸 A SPECIAL INVITATION TO OUR ESTABLISHED AFRIKANER FRIENDS!

Just because you arrived in America as a refugee doesn’t mean you cannot become an American Neighbor yourself!

If you have settled into your new life, are doing well, and are planning to celebrate Thanksgiving, we would love for you to consider joining the American Neighbor Network.

Perhaps you could welcome another Afrikaner family to your Thanksgiving table, help a newly arrived family navigate their community, or simply offer the friendship and encouragement that you may have appreciated when you first arrived.

You understand the journey because you’ve walked it yourself. Now you have an opportunity to help someone else along the way.

Our American Neighbor Network is about building a community where everyone has something meaningful to contribute.

📋 IMPORTANT REGISTRATION REQUIREMENT

All Afrikaner families wishing to receive Thanksgiving assistance through this initiative must first be registered with The Bridge to Liberty.

Once registered, families can sign in using their Bridge to Liberty registration number and password to select their Thanksgiving participation option.

American Neighbor Network volunteers who wish to host or assist must also complete the appropriate volunteer registration process.

📅 IMPORTANT DATES

🍂 Registration Opens: October 21, 2026

🌾 Registration Closes: November 8, 2026

🦃 Thanksgiving Day: November 26, 2026

All Thanksgiving assistance is subject to available funding, eligibility, and local arrangements.

Americans and established Afrikaner refugees can participate by welcoming a family, assisting with meal delivery, or contributing toward Thanksgiving meals.

Thanksgiving is more than a meal. It is an opportunity to thank God for His blessings, share what we have, and extend friendship to those around us.

Our hope is that this becomes an annual tradition, creating relationships that last long after Thanksgiving Day.

Two Homelands. Shared Faith. One Thanksgiving.

❤️ Faith • Friendship • Gratitude

Learn more, register, or help support a family’s Thanksgiving:

https://t.co/ps1D8LAvFw
Give toward a family's Thanksgiving: https://t.co/lbMafp41ZU

The Bridge to Liberty

text:
His Medal of Honor arrived 37 years after the battle. The deed behind it was the earliest by any African American recipient.

William Harvey Carney was born February 29, 1840, in Norfolk, Virginia, and spent most of his boyhood enslaved. At fourteen he secretly attended a school kept by a minister and learned to read and write. He made his way to freedom in New Bedford, Massachusetts, and thought about entering the ministry. Instead, he later wrote, "I could best serve my God by serving my country and my oppressed brothers."

In February 1863 he enlisted in the 54th Massachusetts, one of the first Black regiments of the war, and was soon a sergeant in Company C.

On July 18, 1863, the 54th led the assault on Fort Wagner, South Carolina. When the color bearer was shot down, Carney threw down his musket, took the flag, and carried it to the parapet. When the attack failed, he brought it back under heavy fire. A musket ball shattered his leg. A shell fragment struck his head. An officer offered to carry the colors. Carney refused. He would give them to no man unless he belonged to the 54th Massachusetts. Back at the lines he told his comrades, "The old flag never touched the ground."

His wounds ended his service in 1864. He carried the mail in New Bedford for 32 years and later worked as a messenger at the Massachusetts State House. The Medal of Honor came in May 1900.

He died December 9, 1908. The flags on the State House flew at half-staff, one of the first times Massachusetts gave that honor to a Black man.

Remember William Harvey Carney.

City Therapeutics ($CTY) shares are due for delivery to investors on or about October 19, 2026, following its upsized initial public offering on the Nasdaq Global Market.

Per the final prospectus, the company sold 11,111,111 shares of common stock at $18.00 per share — up from 9,722,222 shares at a $17.00–$19.00 range in the preliminary prospectus — for $200.0 million in gross proceeds, with an underwriters' option for up to 1,666,666 additional shares from the company.

The structural plumbing across the Four Lines:

1. Primary vs. Secondary Allocation:
All 11,111,111 shares are sold by the company; no existing stockholder sells. Net proceeds are approximately $181.5 million (approximately $209.4 million if the option is exercised in full). The new shares are 21.5% of the 51,721,168 shares outstanding after the offering (23.9% with the option), leaving pre-offering holders with 78.5%. At the offer price, those 51,721,168 shares come to $931.0 million.

2. Debt Repayment and Capital Runway:
The use of proceeds includes no debt repayment, and the company has never declared or paid a cash dividend. Immediately before completion, all convertible preferred stock converts into 28,848,641 common shares and the Biogen convertible note into 2,133,788 shares, at 85% of the offer price. Together with existing cash, the company intends approximately $30.0 million for CITY-FXI (its ongoing Phase 1 trial and the start of a Phase 2 study in knee replacement), $20.0 million for CITY-RBP4, $40.0 million for CITY-TFR2, and $70.0 million for the City Platform and preclinical candidates, with the remainder for working capital. The company believes, based on its current operating plan, that this funds operations into late 2028.

3. Share Classes and Governance:
One class of common stock, one vote per share; 10,000,000 shares of undesignated preferred stock are authorized. Executive officers, directors and 5% holders will beneficially own approximately 51.5% after the offering; the largest holder, ARCH Venture Fund XII, holds 26.0%. The company, its directors and officers, and holders of substantially all of its capital stock are locked up for 180 days from the date of the prospectus.

4. Corporate Architecture:
A Delaware corporation that owns its business directly, with one wholly owned Massachusetts securities subsidiary. The prospectus describes no Up-C structure and no tax receivable agreement.

The multiple is the debate; the structure is the fact.
