Mt. Zion Christian Church in Johnson County, Missouri, was destroyed by a fire before dawn on Wednesday, Oct. 14, according to KCTV5. Firefighters confirmed the building was a total loss. No injuries were reported.

Elder Troy Schroeder arrived around 4:30 a.m. and watched it burn. His words to the station: "𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘣𝘶𝘪𝘭𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨'𝘴 𝘨𝘰𝘯𝘦 𝘣𝘶𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘤𝘩𝘶𝘳𝘤𝘩 𝘪𝘴 𝘴𝘵𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘩𝘦𝘳𝘦."

The congregation has gathered in that spot since 1840. The building itself dated to 1896, with an addition in 2008. That is 𝐦𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝟏𝟖𝟎 𝐲𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 in one rural corner of Missouri, about 60 miles east of Kansas City, through wars, depressions and every hard season in between.

Elder Mark Strickland has attended for 72 years. He put it plainly: "𝘛𝘩𝘦 𝘤𝘩𝘶𝘳𝘤𝘩 𝘪𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘤𝘰𝘯𝘨𝘳𝘦𝘨𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯; 𝘪𝘵'𝘴 𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘣𝘶𝘪𝘭𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨." Neighbors have already offered their own buildings so the congregation can keep meeting.

The Missouri State Fire Marshal is still investigating the cause, and nothing has been announced. Meanwhile, the church says it 𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐫𝐞𝐛𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝, and the community around it is already showing up to help. Nobody here is waiting on a government program to tell them what to do next.

𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐬𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐲, 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐜𝐡𝐮𝐫𝐜𝐡. 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐠𝐫𝐞𝐠𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐥𝐢𝐤𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐥𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐬𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐧 𝐚 𝐟𝐢𝐫𝐞.

text: Young America's Foundation (YAF) @yaf  student chapter at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University's Daytona Beach campus submitted a request to host retired Army Lt. Col. @AllenWest , a combat veteran and former Florida congressman, for an October 27 talk on American freedom and leadership. After days of review emails, Negar Afshar, who directs student organizations, wrote on October 15 that the university was "unable to approve the invitation for former Congressman Allen West at this time." No rule was cited. No security threat was described. The email offered help finding "alternative speakers who align with your goals and our institutional values." This is not the first time. In late 2025, Embry-Riddle's Prescott, Arizona, campus rejected four poster versions for a West appearance that criticized diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI). A complaint with the U.S. Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights cited roughly $62 million in federal dollars on the school's 2024 tax filing. Daytona Beach Reserve Officers' Training Corps (ROTC) programs count nearly 800 cadets and midshipmen. Air Force ROTC Detachment 157 is the second-largest in the nation. Over five years the university has commissioned more than 750 officers. Embry-Riddle is private, but it accepts federal money and hosts federal officer programs. President P. Barry Butler should reverse the decision and approve the October 27 event. The Board of Trustees should adopt one written, viewpoint-neutral standard for student-invited speakers. The Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights should act on the complaint already before it. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth's team should ask how universities that host ROTC detachments treat student groups that invite veterans to speak. See link in comments

•Sunbeam World School: Designed specifically for Gulf Standard Time, providing a full-year online curriculum with structured lessons and assessments. [1]
•Al Noor Virtual School: Provides virtual classes, Quran with Tajweed, spoken English, and general K-12 subject tuition. [1]

Key Things to Know
•Regulation & Expatriates: Expatriate families in Dubai are not legally mandated to use a physical KHDA-registered campus school and can freely choose accredited international online providers. Online-only schools based outside local municipal oversight do not require KHDA registration for expat enrollment. [1]
•Exams: For British curriculum online students (such as Pearson Edexcel or IGCSE/A-Levels), public examinations are typically sat as private candidates through regional centers like the British Council UAE. [1]
•Cost vs. Physical Schools: Annual tuition for online schools typically ranges lower (roughly AED 15,000–30,000 or lower depending on the provider) compared to traditional physical private schools in Dubai (AED 45,000–110,000), with zero transport or campus uniform costs. [1]

text:
Jan Koum grew up in a village outside Kyiv with no running water, immigrated to California at sixteen living on food stamps, and twenty two years later signed a nineteen billion dollar deal on the front door of the exact building where he used to collect that same food stamp assistance.

Koum arrived in Mountain View in 1992 with his mother, escaping a country where he says he grew up afraid that everything he said was being recorded and reported on by the state. His mother worked as a babysitter while he swept floors at a local grocery store and taught himself computer networking from used manuals bought at a secondhand bookstore. He eventually landed a job at Yahoo, where he spent nine years as an infrastructure engineer and met his future business partner Brian Acton. In 2009, after both men were separately rejected for jobs at Facebook, Koum bought an iPhone, noticed how the new App Store was about to change everything, and built a simple, ad free messaging app in about a week, naming it WhatsApp because it sounded like what’s up. Acton invested two hundred fifty thousand dollars of his own savings to become a cofounder, and Sequoia Capital put in a total of sixty million dollars across three funding rounds, the only outside investor the company ever took. Five years later, Facebook offered nineteen billion dollars for a company that was generating just over ten million dollars a year in revenue at the time. Koum, Acton, and their investor from Sequoia drove to the old welfare office on Moffett Boulevard where Koum used to stand in line with his mother for food stamps as a teenager, and signed the deal papers right there on the door.

If a kid who once lined up for food assistance in that exact building could end up signing a nineteen billion dollar deal on its front door less than twenty five years later, how much do you think circumstances really decide where someone eventually ends up?

text:
In December 2008, Elon Musk had less than nine million dollars left in Tesla’s bank account, no house of his own, and was personally borrowing money from friends just to pay his rent.

Musk had already poured more than one hundred million dollars of his own money, nearly everything he made from selling PayPal, into keeping Tesla and SpaceX alive at the same time. SpaceX had failed its first three rocket launches in a row, each one burning through cash the company desperately needed, and Tesla was hemorrhaging money fast enough that Musk later called 2008 the worst year of his entire life, on top of going through a divorce at the exact same time. On December 23rd, 2008, with Tesla just days from running out of money completely, NASA called and awarded SpaceX a one point six billion dollar contract after its fourth launch attempt finally succeeded. The very next day, December 24th, at six in the evening, Tesla closed a forty million dollar financing round in the final hour it was even possible, narrowly avoiding missing payroll just two days later. Musk has said he genuinely believed, at the time, that both companies would still probably fail, and put in the last of his own money anyway because the alternative felt like certain death for everything he had built.

If one of the richest men alive today once had less money in the bank than most people save for a used car, and still refused to quit even when he privately expected to lose everything, how much do you think separates eventual success from simply being the last person willing to keep going?

text:
Sara Blakely had five thousand dollars in savings and a day job selling fax machines door to door when she cut the feet off a pair of pantyhose in her apartment, and twenty one years later she sold her company for one point two billion dollars.

Blakely spent seven years selling fax machines door to door in Florida, getting doors slammed in her face so often that she later joked rejection became her middle name. In 1998, frustrated that she could not find the right undergarment to wear under white pants, she cut the feet off a pair of control top pantyhose herself and realized she might be onto something. She used her entire five thousand dollars in savings to start the company, wrote her own patent application using a book from the library to avoid paying a lawyer, and kept the entire idea secret from her friends and family for a full year because she worried their doubts might talk her out of it before she even started. She personally cold called hosiery mills across the country for months before one finally agreed to manufacture her product. The real turning point came when she sent Oprah Winfrey a gift basket with a handwritten note, and Oprah ended up naming Spanx one of her favorite products of the year on national television. Blakely never took a single outside investor in over two decades of running the company, and in 2021 sold a majority stake in Spanx for one point two billion dollars.

If a woman selling fax machines door to door with five thousand dollars to her name could build a billion dollar company just by paying attention to her own daily frustration, how many ideas do you think the rest of us walk past every single day without ever stopping to notice them?

text:
An Appraisal from the Faculty of Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies
University of California, Berkeley
On the Cinematic Nostos of Christopher Nolan

Dear Mr. Nolan,

As one who has long contemplated the living pulse of the epic upon the stage and screen from the ancient dithyrambs to the darkened auditorium of our own time I write to you from the hills of Berkeley with a measure of scholarly admiration and theatrical recognition.

Your recent labors in the art of the moving image have already marked you as a modern craftsman of metis, that cunning intelligence the Greeks prized above mere strength. In Oppenheimer you rendered the terrible birth of a new fire with a precision that recalled the hubris of those who dared the gods; now, in your debut upon the wine-dark seas of Homer’s Odyssey, you have undertaken something rarer still: the full cinematic embodiment of nostos, the fraught return.

A Mythic Invocation

Sing to me of the man, Muse, the man of twists and turns  
driven time and again off course, once he had plundered  
the hallowed heights of Troy.  
Many cities of men he saw and learned their minds,  
many pains he suffered, heartsick on the open sea,  
fighting to save his life and bring his comrades home.
Homer, The Odyssey, Book I (Fagles translation)

You have answered that ancient call not with mere spectacle, but with a fidelity to the human cost of the journey. Matt Damon’s Odysseus is no invulnerable demigod; he is the middle-aged wanderer whose cunning is tempered by loss, whose longing for Penelope (so finely embodied by Anne Hathaway) and for the son who has grown in his absence (Tom Holland’s Telemachus) gives the epic its true gravity. To shoot such a tale almost entirely on IMAX film—eschewing the digital illusions that so often distance us from the body—is itself an act of theatrical integrity. It returns the epic to the scale of the living eye and the breathing voice.

On the Art of the Return

In the tradition of our department, we teach that performance is always a negotiation between the inherited myth and the present moment. Your Odyssey does precisely this. The gods are felt more than seen; Athena’s guidance arrives as strategic clarity rather than spectacle; the Cyclops and the Sirens become trials of perception and restraint. This is not a departure from Homer so much as a rediscovery of his core concern: that a man may survive the war only to face the harder labor of becoming himself again amid the ruins of home.

Your earlier works prepared the way. The fragmented memory of Memento, the nested dreams of Inception, the temporal fractures of Interstellar and Dunkirk—all were, in their fashion, odysseys of the mind. Now you have given us the archetype itself, and in doing so you have revealed how those earlier films were always circling the same Ithaca.

A Closing Word

The Muse, once invoked, does not guarantee a safe harbor; she only promises that the story will be told with the necessary force. In your hands, the tale has been told with both grandeur and intimacy. For this—and for the reminder that cinema, at its highest, remains a form of theater in which we still recognize the old gods and the older human longing—we offer this appraisal with the respect due a true dramatist of the contemporary epic.

May your next voyage, whatever sea it crosses, be guided by the same clear-eyed craft.

With esteem,  
Professor of Theater Arts  
Department of Theater, Dance, and Performance Studies  
University of California, Berkeley

text:
One compromised login exposed California students' personal records.

Millions of students could be affected.

And the scary part? The attackers didn't need to break through every security system. They used a login credential that had already been compromised.

On October 19, SecurityWeek reported a data breach involving Educational Testing Service (ETS), an organization that handles state-mandated testing for California schools.

Let's talk about what actually happened.

First, what was ETS doing with students' data?

ETS works with California's Department of Education to support statewide testing programs.

To exchange student assessment records with the department, ETS used a system called SFTP.

SFTP stands for Secure File Transfer Protocol. Think of it as a protected digital delivery system that allows organizations to transfer files between computers.

But here's the problem: even a secure file-transfer system can be abused if someone gets access using valid login credentials.

How did the breach happen?

According to the official investigation:

September 25, 2026: ETS detected unauthorized activity on its file-transfer system.

But the intrusion had started much earlier.

Investigators found that someone used a compromised login credential to access the system at different times between May 22 and September 18.

The intruder copied files containing California student information.

That means the activity went on for months before it was detected.

But how did the attacker get the login details?

This is where we need to be careful.

The official disclosure has not explained how the credentials were compromised.

It could be tempting to blame phishing, password theft or another attack method, but there is no confirmed evidence identifying the exact cause.

What we know is that the attacker had access to a legitimate login credential and used it without authorization.

This is one reason stolen credentials are so dangerous: an attacker can appear to be a legitimate user.

What information was exposed?

The copied records may include:

• Students' names, dates of birth and home addresses.

• Their schools, districts and grade levels.

• Student identification numbers.

• Race or ethnicity, primary language and country of origin.

• Disability status and testing accommodations.

• English proficiency information and test registration or results.

Not every student's record contained all these details.

The official notice says Social Security numbers, passwords, financial account details and parents' or guardians' personal information were not involved.

How many people were affected?

The exact number has not been publicly confirmed.

However, the incident affects more than just current students. The official notice says it may include students who attended California public schools in recent school years, as well as former students who left as far back as 2006 without a confirmed transfer recorded by the department.

Millions of records could be involved, but we should not mistake California's total student population for a confirmed number of victims.

What happened after the breach was discovered?

ETS disabled the compromised account and took the affected file-transfer site offline.

It began building a replacement system with stronger security controls.

The company also worked with law enforcement and cybersecurity experts. As of the official update, monitoring had not found evidence that the stolen information had been published publicly.

Affected current and former students are being offered two years of free identity-protection services.

What can we learn from this?

This incident is a reminder that cybersecurity is not just about preventing hackers from breaking into a system.

It's also about protecting accounts, limiting what each account can access, monitoring suspicious activity and detecting abuse quickly.

For organizations:

• Use multi-factor authentication wherever possible.

• Give accounts access only to the information they need.

• Monitor login activity and unusual file downloads.

• Review access permissions regularly.

• Alert security teams when an account behaves differently from normal.

For everyday users, remember that personal information can be used to make scam messages more convincing.

If someone knows your school, name, location or other personal details, that does not automatically mean their message is legitimate.

Verify unexpected requests before sharing more information.

The biggest lesson?

A system can have security protections and still be compromised when an attacker gains access through a legitimate account.

And sometimes, the longer an intrusion goes unnoticed, the more information an attacker has time to copy.

Source: California Department of Education

People were moving from out of state, buying and renting homes for an assignment in the brand new San Quentin Prison Psychiatric hospital only to find out that they had no job when the death row Prisoners were sent to General Population and the San Quention Psychiatric Hospital Project was abandoned for lack of funding....

That is the Back Story to this post.
I was in the habit of photographing sunrises on the way to work and sunsets in the evening to start and end the day with meditation on peace and beauty...just saying...again...what say you?

Shared with Your friends
I drive to work every morning watching the sun rise. A great way to to start the day.

You're all caught up
Check back tomorrow to see more of your memories!

Thought for 24s
Lecture: Institutional Collapse, Personal Continuity, and the Optics of Chaos
A Multidisciplinary Examination of the Abandoned San Quentin Death-Row Psychiatric Hospital Project (2014)
For Graduate Students in Law, Political Science, Psychiatry, and Social Anthropology
Opening Context

On the morning of 19 October 2014, 
a traveling contract psychiatrist 
drove toward San Quentin State Priso
n photographing the sunrise. 

The image and caption 
that later resurfaced 
as a Facebook memory 
read simply: 

“I drive to work every morning
 watching the sun rise. 
A great way to start the day.” 

Behind that ordinary ritual 
lay an institutional drama. 

A court-ordered, 
federally overseen 
psychiatric hospital 
dedicated to death-row prisoners 
was under construction. 

Recruiters 
had sought clinicians nationwide. 

Individuals and families 
relocated, 
leased or purchased housing, 
and arranged their professional lives 
around the promised facility. 

Then the project was abandoned 
for lack of funding; 
death-row prisoners 
were returned to general population. 

Many of those 
who had moved 
found themselves 
without the positions t
hey had been promised. 

The psychiatrist in question, 
working as a 1099 independent contractor, 
simply boarded a plane 
for a preexisting backup assignment 
at a prison in Ionia, Michigan, 
and missed no days of work. 

The sunrise photographs continued.

This episode supplies 
a compact case 
for examining 
how large public institutions 
generate, 
absorb, 
and redistribute 
uncertainty. 

The lenses requested
—plausible deniability, 
self-organizing systems,
 Pandora’s Box, 
Murphy’s Law, 
and the Butterfly Effect
—are not metaphors 
imposed from outside; 

they describe 
observable dynamics 
in the 
legal, 
political, 
clinical, and 
anthropological 
registers of the event.

Plausible Deniability

In administrative and legal practice, 
plausible deniability 
is the structural capacity 
of an actor 
or institution 
to disclaim 
knowledge 
or responsibility 
after the fact. 

The court order 
and federal oversight 
created an affirmative duty; 
the subsequent funding shortfall 
supplied a clean external cause. 

No single official 
needed to have “intended” 
the dislocation of out-of-state clinicians. 

Budget cycles, 
legislative appropriations, 
and inter-agency coordination 
could each be cited 
as the point 
at which responsibility dissolved. 

For law students 
this raises classic questions 
of proximate cause, 
sovereign immunity, 
and the enforceability 
of employment expectations 
created by public recruitment. 

For political scientists 
it illustrates 
how multi-level governance 
multiplies veto points 
while diffusing accountability. 

Psychiatrists 
recognize the same pattern 
inside clinical organizations: 
a mandate 
for specialized care is issued, 
then quietly withdrawn, 
leaving 
residual ethical obligations 
without corresponding resources. 

Anthropologists 
observe that plausible deniability 
is also a cultural technology
—ritualized language 
(“lack of funding,” 
“change in operational priorities”) 
that allows institutions 
to continue functioning 
while participants 
absorb the costs 
of broken promises.

Self-Organizing Systems

Complex adaptive systems 
exhibit order 
without central design. 

The recruitment process itself 
was only partially centralized. 

Clinicians across states 
evaluated the opportunity, 
calculated risk, 
and moved. 

Informal networks
—professional listservs, 
word-of-mouth among traveling psychiatrists, 
local real-estate agents near San Quentin
—coordinated 
housing 
and logistics 
faster than any official plan. 

Once the hospital was abandoned, 
the same decentralized capacities 
reasserted themselves. 

Some individuals 
renegotiated contracts; 
others exited the prison system entirely. 

The 1099 contractor 
who already maintained 
a secondary assignment 
exemplifies minimal 
but decisive self-organization: 
redundancy 
was built into the personal career structure 
rather than into the institutional one.

 In psychiatric terms 
this resembles the difference 
between 
a rigidly programmed treatment protocol 
and a clinician’s capacity 
for real-time reformulation 
when the protocol collapses. 

In anthropological terms 
it is the ordinary competence 
of mobile professionals 
who treat institutions 
as environments 
rather than as permanent homes.

Pandora’s Box

A judicial mandate 
to provide specialized psychiatric care 
for a condemned population 
opens a container 
whose contents cannot 
be fully inventoried in advance. 

The box 
contains clinical standards, 
staffing models, 
architectural requirements, 
political symbolism, 
and the private hopes 
of people who accept offers. 

Once opened, 
the contents 
cannot be returned 
simply by closing the lid. 

Expectations of 
employment, 
family relocation, 
and professional identity 
have already been released 
into the world. 

The subsequent funding failure 
does not 
restore the status quo ante; 
it leaves 
residual obligations, 
disappointed claimants, 
and a precedent 
that future court order
s will be discounted. 

Law students 
will recognize the problem 
of remedial decrees 
that outrun 
the political will 
to fund them. 

Political scientists
 see the classic gap 
between rights declaration a
nd resource allocation. 

Clinicians confront 
the ethical residue: 
patients who were told 
a specialized unit was coming, 
staff who were told 
their expertise was needed. 

Anthropologists note 
that once a sacred 
or high-stakes category 
(death row, psychiatric necessity) 
is ritually elevated, 
its later demotion 
produces lasting cultural damage 
to trust in the institution.

Murphy’s Law

“Anything that can go wrong will go wrong” 
is less a prophecy 
than a description 
of tightly coupled systems 
operating under resource constraints 
and multiple veto points. 

Large capital projects 
inside correctional systems 
are especially vulnerable: 
construction timelines, 
legislative appropriations, 
union agreements, 
security classifications, 
and clinical credentialing 
must all align. 

The probability 
that any single element fails is high; 
the probability 
that at least one fails 
is near certainty. 

In this case the failure mode
—funding
—was both foreseeable and, o
nce it occurred, 
decisive. 

Graduate students in all four fields 
can treat Murphy’s Law 
as a planning heuristic 
rather than fatalism: 
design for graceful degradation, 
maintain parallel options, 
and avoid single points of failure. 

The contractor who already possessed 
a Michigan assignment 
had, 
in effect, 
built a personal fail-safe 
against precisely this class 
of institutional risk.

The Butterfly Effect

Small differences 
in initial conditions 
produce divergent trajectories. 

The decision 
to classify death-row prisoners 
as eligible for a dedicated psychiatric hospital, r
ather than for enhanced services 
inside existing units, s
et in motion hiring cascades, 
interstate moves, 
and real-estate transactions. 

A subsequent budgetary decision
—itself the product 
of many smaller political calculations
—reversed the cascade. 

For the individuals 
who had already relocated, 
the difference between 
“project proceeds” 
and “project cancelled” 
was the difference 
between a multi-year professional commitment 
and an abrupt exit. 

The same sensitivity 
appears at the personal scale: 
the choice to maintain 1099 status 
and a secondary contract 
converted an institutional reversal 
into a same-day flight 
rather than unemployment. 

Daily sunrise photography, 
repeated across months, 
is a still smaller perturbation 
whose cumulative effect 
is a sustained attentional practice
—attention to light, 
weather, 
and the road
—independent of the institutional weather.

Synthesis Across Disciplines

Law 
supplies the formal triggers 
(court order, oversight) 
and the residual liability questions. 

Political science 
maps the veto points 
and funding discontinuities 
that convert formal rights 
into practical nullities. 

Psychiatry must reckon 
with both the clinical population 
that was briefly promised specialized care 
and the workforce 
whose own stability was collateral damage. 

Social anthropology 
tracks the human-scale adaptations
—relocation, 
renegotiation, 
ritual (sunrise watching)
—through which people 
reconstitute order 
when formal systems retract. 

The five lenses are not alternative explanations; 
they are successive magnifications 
of the same process. 

Plausible deniability 
explains how responsibility is shed; 
self-organization 
explains how people continue; 
Pandora’s Box 
explains why the shed responsibility 
still has consequences; 
Murphy’s Law 
explains why the failure was probable; 
the Butterfly Effect 
explains why the consequences 
were unevenly distributed.

The sunrise photograph is not incidental. 

It is a low-cost, 
repeatable practice 
that remains available 
when institutional arrangements do not. 

In a system characterized 
by deniability, 
coupling failures, 
and sensitive dependence 
on initial conditions, 
the capacity to begin the day 
by attending to something 
that does not require institutional permission 
is itself a form of resilience. 

That practice 
neither denies the chaos 
nor pretends to control it; 
it simply continues.

Poem
(after the rhythmic, direct-address, slightly weary groove of Bill Withers’ “Use Me”)

Use the sunrise, baby,
use the light on the road.
Take what the system won’t keep
and use me up, use me up.

Plausible deniability
walked away clean,
left the keys on the table,
said the money was gone.

You can use that story,
use it till it’s worn,
I already bought the ticket,
I already made the phone.

Self-organizing, honey,
that’s just how we move—
no memo, no meeting,
just the plane and the groove.

Murphy wrote the contract,
Pandora signed the line,
butterfly flapped in Sacramento
and I landed on time.

Use the morning, baby,
use the gray and the pink.
Take the court order’s promise
and the funding that sank.

I’m still driving, still watching,
still starting the day—
you can use every color
the sky decides to make.

Use me for the witness,
use me for the proof
that the box stays open
even after the roof
falls in on the project,
falls in on the plan.

I’ll be in Michigan by evening
with the same steady hand.
So use the sunrise,
use the quiet, use the miles.

Whatever the institution
decides to reconcile—
I’ll be there at the window
when the light starts to climb,
using what is left
to get through one more time.

text:
THE BASTILLE: BETWEEN VANDALISM AND FOUNDATION—THE QUESTION THAT CANNOT BE AVOIDED

THE ACT AND THE SYMBOL

On July 14, 1789, an armed crowd stormed the Bastille—a fortress and prison that, for decades, had embodied the arbitrary nature of royal power in the collective imagination. Contemporary accounts describe a siege, a surrender, and the subsequent killing of the governor, de Launay, as he was being led toward the Hôtel de Ville. This was no peaceful demonstration; it was an act of collective violence that, by today’s legal standards, would constitute several criminal offenses. This is not a retroactive moral judgment; it is a statement of fact.

THE PARADOX OF THE DECLARATION

A few weeks later, on August 26, 1789, the National Assembly approved the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen—a text that remains in force in France to this day. Article 2 defines "resistance to oppression" as a natural and imprescriptible right. The chronological link is undeniable: the Declaration emerged in the wake of that violent summer. The question that arises is not merely rhetorical; it is the central question for any political order: who decides where legitimate resistance ends and crime begins?

THE ANSWER LIES IN POWER, NOT MORALITY

The transformation of an act of vandalism into a foundational event is no philosophical mystery. It is a matter of power dynamics. The Bastille became a symbol because the revolutionaries won, and because that symbol served to legitimize the new order. Had the same act been carried out by a group that ultimately lost, it would have been dismissed as a criminal riot. History offers no examples of failed revolutions that are celebrated as legitimate foundations by those who emerge victorious. The moral label—whether "vandal" or "founding father"—is assigned in retrospect by those who hold the power to craft the narrative.

THE REMAINING PROBLEM

This does not mean that all forms of violence are equivalent, nor that the Declaration of 1789 is devoid of value. It means that the foundation of a political order does not rest upon an original moral purity, but rather upon an act of force—an act that morality is subsequently called upon to justify. A few years later, Robespierre would explicitly theorize that "terror is nothing other than justice, prompt, severe, and inflexible." That logic was already present in the summer of 1789. Recognizing this is not cynicism; it is a prerequisite for avoiding its uncritical repetition.

text:
What To Do If HR Rejects You Because You Wake Up Late

If an interviewer explicitly links your rejection to your usual wake-up time, consider the following steps.

1. Ask For Clarification. Determine whether the concern was your actual availability or merely your personal routine.

2. Review The Advertised Working Hours. Check whether you met the stated scheduling requirements.

3. Request Job-Related Feedback. Ask which requirement you were considered unable to meet.

4. Avoid Assuming Unlawful Discrimination. An unfair or poorly reasoned decision is not automatically illegal.

5. Preserve Relevant Communications. Keep the job advertisement and any written explanations.

6. Assess Whether The Schedule Was Realistic. Be truthful with yourself about your ability to meet the position's requirements.

7. Consider Whether The Employer Is A Good Fit. An organization that judges candidates through irrelevant personal stereotypes may not offer a healthy working environment.

8. Improve Your Future Responses. Explain your actual availability more clearly.

9. Continue Exploring Other Opportunities. Don't let one employer's decision determine your career prospects.

10. Seek Advice If Necessary. If the rejection appears connected to unlawful discrimination or another protected issue, consider appropriate professional guidance.

The Biggest Secret About This Interview Question

The strongest candidates don't try to impress HR by claiming they wake up earlier than everyone else.

They understand that waking up early and being ready for work are two different things.

Consider two employees:

Employee A wakes up at 5:00 AM, arrives late three times a week, and regularly misses deadlines.

Employee B wakes up at 7:30 AM, reports to work at the agreed time, and consistently meets performance expectations.

Which employee is more reliable?

Clearly, Employee B.

The lesson is that the employer should evaluate actual performance and attendance, not make assumptions based on personal routines.

text:
How To Identify And Avoid A Toxic Workplace Culture 

A question about waking up early is not automatically a warning sign. 

However, the interviewer's reaction can reveal how the company treats employee boundaries. 

Watch for these signs: 

1. Management Equates Early Rising With Loyalty. They believe employees who wake up earlier are automatically better workers. 

2. Unpaid Early Arrivals Are Expected. Employees are pressured to report before their scheduled hours without appropriate compensation. 

3. Working Hours Are Unclear. HR refuses to explain when employees are expected to start and finish. 

4. Unlimited Availability Is Expected. Managers assume employees should be available at any hour. 

5. Personal Routines Are Micromanaged. The company tries to control employees' private schedules unnecessarily. 

6. Long Working Hours Are Celebrated. Management treats exhaustion as evidence of dedication. 

7. Employees Are Shamed For Resting. Workers are criticized for maintaining reasonable sleep and recovery routines. 

8. Schedules Change Without Proper Notice. Employees are expected to accommodate sudden changes without reasonable consideration. 

9. Performance Is Measured By Presence Rather Than Results. Management values being seen at work more than meaningful productivity. 

10. Candidates Are Pressured To Reveal Unnecessary Personal Information. HR treats reasonable requests for clarification as disobedience. 

A healthy employer should care whether you can meet your agreed working hours, not whether you wake up earlier than everyone else. 

How To Survive If You Already Work Under A Boss Who Controls Your Morning Routine 

Some employees discover after joining a company that management expects them to wake up unusually early, arrive before their shift, or remain available outside working hours. 

Here's how to handle it strategically. 

1. Review Your Employment Contract 

Confirm your official working hours, shift arrangements, and any applicable flexibility requirements. 

2. Separate Reporting Time From Wake-Up Time 

Your employer may legitimately require you to report at 8:00 AM. 

That doesn't ordinarily mean your manager needs to dictate whether you wake up at 5:00 AM or 7:00 AM. 

3. Meet Your Agreed Working Hours 

Consistent punctuality helps establish your reliability. 

4. Request Written Clarification Of Schedule Changes 

If management introduces earlier reporting times, ask for confirmation of the new arrangement. 

5. Document Unpaid Work Expectations 

Maintain appropriate records if you're repeatedly required to perform work outside scheduled hours. 

6. Avoid Sharing Unnecessary Personal Details 

You don't need to explain your entire morning routine every time your manager discusses punctuality. 

7. Protect Your Rest 

Don't routinely sacrifice sleep to satisfy unreasonable expectations. 

8. Raise Concerns Professionally 

If working hours become excessive or unpredictable, explain the impact and request a workable arrangement. 

9. Understand Your Employment Rights 

Working-time limits, overtime rules, rest periods, and scheduling protections vary by jurisdiction. 

10. Maintain Alternative Employment Options 

If the company consistently disregards reasonable boundaries, keep your resume updated and explore other opportunities. 

 How To Stay Ahead Of HR And Management 

Highly strategic employees don't wait until workplace expectations become unreasonable before establishing clarity. 

1. Confirm Working Hours Before Accepting The Offer. Ask about the exact start time, end time, and break arrangements. 

2. Ask Whether Shifts Rotate. Understand how frequently your schedule may change. 

3. Clarify Overtime Expectations. Determine whether additional hours are required and how they are compensated. 

4. Understand Remote-Work Availability Rules. Know whether employees must be online at fixed times. 

5. Ask About Schedule Flexibility. Determine whether alternative starting times are available. 

6. Keep Written Records Of Agreed Terms. Preserve relevant offer letters, contracts, and schedule confirmations. 

7. Evaluate Commute Feasibility. Don't accept a schedule you cannot consistently meet. 

8. Avoid Overpromising Availability. Only commit to working arrangements you can realistically maintain. 

9. Build Professional Credibility Through Results. Demonstrate reliability through attendance and performance. 

10. Keep Your Career Options Open. Don't allow one employer to become your only source of professional opportunity. 

 Tips For Highly Intelligent And High-Value Candidates 

1. Never Confuse Waking Up Early With Being Productive 

An employee who wakes up at 5:00 AM is not automatically more productive than someone who wakes up at 9:00 AM. 

Performance depends on many factors, including skills, focus, workload, and working conditions. 

2. Answer The Underlying Employment Question 

If HR is concerned about punctuality, discuss punctuality. 

If HR is concerned about shift availability, discuss availability. 

3. Don't Reveal Personal Information Without A Clear Purpose 

Your private routine may be irrelevant to the position. 

4. Never Lie To Appear More Disciplined 

An impressive-sounding wake-up time is not worth creating unrealistic expectations. 

5. Ask About The Actual Working Schedule 

Know what you're agreeing to before accepting the position. 

6. Recognize When HR Is Testing Unlimited Availability 

Be cautious if the interviewer expects you to be available at all hours without explaining the role's requirements. 

7. Don't Apologize For Having A Personal Life 

Employees can be highly committed professionals while maintaining family responsibilities, hobbies, and adequate rest. 

8. Negotiate Working Arrangements When Appropriate 

If the position permits flexible hours, discuss an arrangement that supports both performance and operational needs. 

9. Maintain Professional Confidence 

You can answer personal questions politely without becoming defensive or submissive. 

10. Evaluate Whether The Employer Respects Boundaries 

A company that values results, clear schedules, and employee well-being is generally preferable to one that equates exhaustion with dedication.

text:
The dust had not yet settled.  

Already the familiar scene of a dream or flashback felt different.  The dust hung low and thick, turning the late light the color of old brass and filling the mouth with the taste of metal and grit.  Instead of a dusty desert corridor, the lead vehicle sits canted ahead, one wheel gone, along a familiar southeast Texas road.

The Duke had not spoken.  No burst across the net, no sudden dead air, nothing to mark that the system had even registered a signal.  Whatever waited on the road had used a wire, a plate, or a frequency the current loadset no longer held.

Yet the failure of the magic bubble was simply the last in a tragedy of errors.  The first was the convoy commander, who was tired.  So worn out that the preplanned forty-five-minute return route was ignored in favor of the same track already driven, now cloaked in the dissipating dust of an explosion.

They stepped off with the spacing training and experience demanded, boots testing the ground for the soft give of a buried plate or the glint of a tripwire.  The compounds that lined the road were close.  In the real place the walls had at least given the eye something solid to measure against.

Here, in the dream, the walls were thinner.  A small desert grouping of buildings had been turned into an RV park with trailers set on cinder blocks and narrow gravel lots, their siding the color of sun-faded cream.  

Then comes the paranoid and prudent realization came that shrapnel and rounds which struck one of these walls would not stop.  They would punch through, carrying fragments with them, and keep going.  There was no solid place to put a shoulder.

A response over the radio, the QRF was still minutes out.  

The radios worked.  The jammers that had failed to stop the first device were not fighting the net this time.  A small mercy to be able to communicate clearly, perhaps, and not much comfort.  Someone was already working the door of the disabled vehicle.  Someone else was already on a knee behind the rear wheels, scanning the trailers for movement that did not belong to the wind or to the slow settling of dust.

They moved the way the training said to move when the cover is not cover.  Low, but not so low that the thin aluminum could not still be crossed by a round that had already come through something else.  The memory wasn’t playing out the way it had countless times before.

The five-meter check was quick because the ground itself offered little to hide.  The twenty-five took longer.  Every trailer window had to be accounted for.  Every door that hung open had to be treated as a place a man could already be standing, rifle up, waiting for the next silhouette to step into the gap.

Where were the people?  Work?  School?  Where am I, when am I?  Already the edges of the dream fray and warp, unable to withstand the scrutiny.

The thin metal siding made a high, thin sound when it was struck, different from the deeper crack of brick or the wet slap of mud.  It was a sound that told the men clearing it that whatever they put between themselves and the next shot would not stay there long enough to matter.  The spaces between the units became lanes.  These lanes became an obstacle course of death that had been built for someone else and then left for us to finish.

The QRF still had not arrived.  The Duke still had not explained itself.  The route that should have been different was the route they were on, and the only way off it now was through the thin places where a man could see daylight on the far side of the wall he was trying to use for cover.

Keep moving.

Darkness.

Jolting up to sweat and the thin light of another Texas morning.  A clock on the far wall, with the date and time.  Slowly putting together another wake-up from a dream-altered memory.

The recall of the real, and how the dream had worked to put the event into southeast Texas.  A trailer park ten or fifteen minutes away from home.  From the house I’m in now.

May as well get up, make some coffee.  Try to shake the dream.

text:
Monday, October 19, 2026 - A Fresh Attitude for a New Day
Good morning, friends. May God refresh your heart and give you strength for today.
I hope you are doing well and will have a good day.
Since 1986, I have officially called these words my motto, although I tried to live by much of their meaning for about 10 years before that:
“A positive mental attitude, to encourage, serve, and inspire others, will motivate me to do my best.”
I share that motto every so often because I need the reminder myself. I also hope it helps and encourages someone else. Today, I needed to hear it again. Perhaps you need a little refreshing in your attitude, too.
“This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.” Psalm 118:24
“And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.”Galatians 6:9
Some mornings, encouragement comes easily. Other mornings, we wake up tired, concerned or unsure how we will manage the day. On those mornings, we can bring our feelings honestly to God and ask Him to help us take the next step.
A positive attitude grows stronger when we ground it in faith. We recognize the difficulties before us while remembering that God walks with us through them. His presence gives us reasons for hope, even when our circumstances remain difficult.
Reflection
Encouraging, serving and inspiring others often begins with something small: a kind word, a thoughtful message, a listening ear or a quiet prayer. We may never know how much that simple act means to someone.
Doing our best will look different from day to day. God knows our strength and our limitations. Today, we can offer Him what we have and trust Him to work through it.
As we begin this Monday, let us ask: Who could use some encouragement? How can I serve with the strength God gives me today?
Prayer
Heavenly Father, thank You for this new day. Refresh our minds and renew our hope. When we feel weary, give us strength. When discouragement settles in, remind us of Your faithful care. Help us encourage, serve and inspire others with kindness and humility. Guide our words and actions so that we honour You and do our best with what You give us today. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
Go into today with hope in God, kindness in your words and a willingness to encourage someone along the way.

text:
🇮🇷|Sarakhs: How a Railway Renders the Term Sanctions Geographically Irrelevant

Standing at the Sarakhs border crossing, Ali Akbar Pourjamshidian, Deputy Interior Minister for Security and Police Affairs, made a remark that might easily be overlooked in a standard press release. He said, "Under current conditions, all of Iran's land border crossings are of vital importance for securing essential goods. Sarakhs, however, possesses a distinct advantage: its railway infrastructure and its connection to East Asia."

This was not a perfunctory comment made during an inspection. It was a strategic assessment.

Why Railways, and Why East Asia

Iran maintains land border crossings with several nations, including Turkey, Iraq, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Armenia, and Turkmenistan. Yet Pourjamshidian specifically highlighted the railway infrastructure at Sarakhs and its link to East Asia.

Located in northeastern Iran along the border with Turkmenistan, Sarakhs serves as a critical node in the Iran Turkmenistan Kazakhstan China railway corridor. This corridor provides the physical foundation for transforming Iran's land routes from mere conduits for regional trade into a backbone for intercontinental logistics.

When a nation faces maritime blockades, financial sanctions, and restrictions on air travel, railways offer a unique mode of transport. It requires neither the permission of the US Navy, nor access to the SWIFT clearing system, nor settlement in US dollars. Trains do not need to pass through the Strait of Hormuz. They do not need to dodge missiles in the Red Sea. They do not need to wait for insurance approvals to navigate the Persian Gulf. All that is required are tracks, railcars, and two neighboring governments willing to grant passage.

The Weight of the Phrase Current Conditions

The term used by Pourjamshidian was current conditions.

What are these current conditions? Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is effectively paralyzed. Insurance premiums for transit through the Red Sea are skyrocketing. The US Fifth Fleet continues to enforce a blockade in the Persian Gulf. Iranian oil tankers in the Gulf of Oman have been switching off their tracking devices in an attempt to circumvent sanctions. Meanwhile, Iran's aviation sector has been unable to procure necessary spare parts due to these same sanctions.

Under these current conditions, with maritime shipping unreliable, air transport restricted, and financial channels severed, land routes have become the only viable option. Among these, rail transport stands out as the most scalable, stable, and resilient mode, and the least susceptible to the impact of sanctions.

The railway at Sarakhs is not merely a project for trade facilitation. It is essential infrastructure for survival under a sanctions regime.

Where Does This Railway Lead

Sarakhs serves as a gateway to East Asia, specifically to China.

China is Iran's largest trading partner, with Iranian oil flowing to China and Chinese industrial goods moving to Iran. Under sanctions, this trade has relied on a shadow fleet, tankers with disabled tracking systems, ship to ship transfers, and intermediaries based in Malaysia and Hong Kong.

However, every link in this maritime chain is subject to tracking, interception, and sanctions by the United States. Tankers are blacklisted, shipowners are issued warnings, insurance companies face threats, and ports are placed under pressure.

The railway offers an alternative route: from China, passing through Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan, and entering Iran at Sarakhs. This path bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, avoids waters patrolled by the US Navy, and eliminates the need for ship to ship transfers at anchorages like those in Malaysia.

Every railcar on this line serves as a physical negation of the very concept of sanctions.

Sarakhs Is Not the Only Node

Iran is simultaneously developing multiple land based corridors.

To the north, a route through Turkmenistan and Kazakhstan, reaching China and Russia, with Sarakhs serving as the gateway.
To the west, a route through Iraq to Syria and Lebanon, providing access to the eastern Mediterranean coast.
To the south, connections to ports on the Gulf of Oman and the Indian Ocean, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz.
To the east, a route through Pakistan to South Asia, linking to the port of Gwadar and the China Pakistan Economic Corridor.

This is not a Look East policy. Rather, it is the simultaneous construction of pathways in all directions, pathways that do not rely on Washington. Each such route diminishes the efficacy of sanctions. Each one helps redefine Iran from a besieged nation into a corridor nation that connects all points of the compass.

What Pourjamshidian Did Not Say

He did not claim that rail transport can entirely replace maritime shipping. It cannot. The capacity of railways is far lower than that of oil tankers, and the costs are significantly higher. Furthermore, rail transport requires the cooperation of neighboring countries, countries that may themselves be subject to pressure from the United States.

Yet he pointed to something more fundamental. When sanctions slam every door shut, one must open whatever window remains, and the railway at Sarakhs is precisely that window.

An open window is far harder to close again than a wall that has been breached. The window frame is already in place, the tracks are laid, and the trains are already running. Sanctions may be able to intercept an oil tanker, but they cannot intercept an operational railway. They can only watch as train after train crosses the border, rendering the very concept of sanctions geographically meaningless, little more than scrap paper.

text:
Tesla has officially announced that it will hold its annual shareholder meeting on December 3, 2026. There are three items up for a vote:

• Re-electing Elon Musk, Robyn Denholm and JB Straubel to the board for three-year terms.
• A non-binding say-on-pay vote on 2025 executive compensation. The compensation table lists about $158.4 billion in 2025 stock awards for Musk.
• Approving PWC as Tesla's auditor for 2026.

There is no mention of any merger with SpaceX in this proxy filing. Letter from Tesla Chair of the Board, Robyn Denholm:

"Dear Fellow Shareholders,
2026 has been a year of investment and progress for Tesla. We continued solidifying our foundation by strengthening our core vehicle, energy and services businesses as we build the infrastructure for our next phase of growth. 

We also moved closer to a future of autonomous transportation and real-world super intelligence (“SI”). This year, we began producing Cybercab at Gigafactory Texas and expanded our Robotaxi service to more U.S. cities. FSD (Supervised) usage grew exponentially as we continued to gain users and expand into new markets. We surpassed over 10 million vehicles delivered, and the Model Y remains on track to be the best-selling vehicle this year of any kind, globally, as we achieved record deliveries in countries around the world. We launched the Tesla Semi, which will revolutionize the trucking industry, and unveiled the long- awaited Next Gen Roadster. We also made progress in energy generation and storage, with record deployments out of Megafactory Shanghai and production of the new Megapack 3 at our Megafactory in Texas. As SI infrastructure demand increases, energy storage will be critical to expand capacity from the existing grid.

At the same time, we continued developing the products and investing in the infrastructure required to provide them at scale, including building our Semi factory in Nevada and the first production lines for Optimus, and additional data center capacity to train our SI systems. Our recent investments in battery and  chip manufacturing, including our Terafab initiative, will help secure the supply of critical components enabling us to offer products affordably on a mass market basis so that humanity may benefit. We remain focused on managing costs and maintaining the financial strength to support our ambitious long-term goals. 

We have accomplished a great deal, but we are still at the early stages of what we believe Tesla can become. Our employees’ innovation, hard work and dedication are essential to realizing that potential and creating lasting value for you, our shareholders. Your confidence in Tesla means a great deal to us, and we take the trust of our shareholders seriously. We listen to you, as your voices and votes help shape our governance and our future. And, as a Board, we want to continue hearing from as many of you as possible. 

That includes retail investors, who face technological barriers to traditional voting. As a result, Tesla recently pioneered the creation of user-friendly practical tools to empower the voices of retail shareholders, which provide a no-fee, investor-directed voting process similar to those currently available to institutional investors. And because we believe all retail voices should be heard across the capital markets, we have made sure the framework supporting enrollment into voluntary retail voting programs would not only be available to Tesla, but to all public companies. As we look ahead, we have the building blocks, vision and team necessary to achieve our bold yet worthwhile objectives. I am honored to serve on the Board alongside Elon Musk and JB Straubel, two technological visionaries whose leadership has helped make Tesla what it is today. The three of us are grateful to have been nominated to serve for another term on the Board of this extraordinary company. We understand that a steady and experienced hand during this time of rapid technological change is essential to Tesla’s success. Therefore, your vote is critical to maintaining that leadership, and I ask you to vote FOR our re-election to the Board so we can continue guiding Tesla through our next phase of growth. 

We have transformed numerous industries before, ranging from electric vehicles to battery storage systems. We could not be more excited to do it again, as we bring SI into the physical world. The best is yet to come.

Thank you for your continued support of Tesla. Very truly yours,
Robyn Denholm
Chair of the Board"

text:
Abdul El-Sayed told a reporter yesterday that scrutiny of him is “the same thing that they did to JFK when he ran for president… the notion that because he was Catholic, that somehow he had dual loyalty.”

I have written about JFK. That claim is a grotesque perversion of history.

In 1960, no Catholic had ever been elected president. Al Smith’s 1928 landslide loss was driven in large part by Protestant fears—rooted in centuries of Reformation conflict and reinforced by nativist suspicion—that a Catholic president would answer to the Vatican rather than the Constitution. JFK met it head-on in Houston in 1960, pledging absolute separation of church and state, and the charge collapsed because there was nothing under it.

That is not what is happening with El-Sayed. 

Being Muslim is not the disqualifier. Keith Ellison, the first Muslim elected to Congress, serves as Minnesota’s attorney general. Ilhan Omar and Rashida Tlaib serve in the House. Zohran Mamdani is mayor of New York City. CAIR’s own 2026 directory counts roughly 255 Muslim elected officials nationwide, including four in the House and dozens in state legislatures. Voters have repeatedly elected Muslims to state and federal office without treating their faith as disqualifying. 

The issue is not prayer; it is politics, associations, and family ties to an ideology that rejects the secular liberal order El-Sayed claims to defend.

El-Sayed flatly denied on Meet the Press any family ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, which the U.S. listed this year as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist entity for material support to Hamas. 

His half-sister, University of Chicago professor Eman Abdelhadi, has posted otherwise. In 2012 she wrote: “My family has long been MB,” though she added that it “navigated the political sphere poorly/destructively.” In 2013 she wrote that she had “family jailed for being a part of it.” She also wrote of her mother’s early-1970s Brotherhood activism in college. Their mother, Fatten Elkomy, later worked for the U.S. arm of a charity network Treasury designated in 2004 for supporting al-Qaeda; she was never charged. 

El-Sayed calls the posts “hearsay” and distances himself from his mother by saying he wasn’t raised by her. But his flat denial and his sister’s own words can’t both be right.

There is more. El-Sayed confirmed on camera that his sister-in-law was on the federal terror watchlist. She sued, a district court ruled in her favor, and an appeals court reversed. The FBI won’t say where she stands now. No one accuses him of any role. His father-in-law is a longtime board member of the Islamic Society of North America.

None of these questions are about how he prays; they are questions about reported links to an organization whose Egyptian branch the United States has now formally labeled for supporting terrorism.

After a man rammed a vehicle into Temple Israel synagogue near Detroit in an attack authorities treated as targeted at Jews, El-Sayed’s response included the line “hurt people hurt people.” He later apologized under pressure from Jewish Democrats, saying he should not have offered “context” that trampled on the victims’ pain. That is not the language of someone simply defending religious freedom.

He has also campaigned repeatedly with Hasan Piker, who in 2019 said “America deserved 9/11.” El-Sayed later called the remark “dumb” and said America did not deserve the attacks, but the association remains. Voters are entitled to notice who a candidate chooses to platform.

JFK faced prejudice against his faith. El-Sayed faces reporting on his family’s documented embrace of a group now designated by the U.S. government for supporting Hamas, his own comments after an attack on a synagogue, and his political alliances. Equating the two is not a defense of religious liberty. It is an attempt to weaponize a real historical injustice in order to shut down legitimate questions about radicalism and national security. The Constitution protects the free exercise of religion. It does not require voters or journalists to pretend that family ties to a designated terrorist organization, or responses to domestic terrorism, are off-limits simply because the candidate is Muslim. History is not a prop for that evasion.

text:
Abdul El-Sayed in Unearthed Synagogue Speech: Hamas Is 'the Same' as the Israeli Military | Chuck Ross, Washington Free Beacon

Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed told a group of Jewish voters at a Detroit synagogue in 2018 that he views the Israeli military "the same way" that he views Hamas, according to video obtained by the Washington Free Beacon.

The left-wing Democrat, speaking at the Isaac Agree Downtown Synagogue in Detroit, offered those thoughts during his failed 2018 gubernatorial campaign when asked about a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

El-Sayed responded with a lengthy sermon about his "values" and "standing up for truth and international law" on "both sides" of the Middle East debate.

"I've always said I'll condemn Hamas and what they do in the same way that I'll condemn some of the human rights abuses that we see on the part of the IDF," El-Sayed said.

At the time, Hamas had for decades been behind terror attacks against Israelis, including many deadly suicide bombings and other murders that targeted children and teens.

El-Sayed told the congregants eight years ago that, as he was running for governor, there would be "very little" he could do about the Israel-Palestinian issue. But now he is running for Senate and is reportedly angling for a spot on the powerful Senate Foreign Relations Committee.

The 2018 video emerges as El-Sayed faces scrutiny over his family's purported ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, the Islamist group that spawned Hamas in Gaza in the 1980s. Eman Abdelhadi, El-Sayed's half-sister with whom he has been close, has stated that their mother and relatives in Egypt have "long been" members of the organization. Abdelhadi has stated that Palestinians have "a right to violent resistance," and she rebuked Sen. Bernie Sanders (I., Vt.), a staunch El-Sayed ally, as a "disappointment" after he condemned the Oct. 7, 2023, attacks.

El-Sayed, who ran heavily against the pro-Israel advocacy group AIPAC in the Democratic primary, has sought to win back historically Democratic Jewish voters who soured on the candidate over his hostility towards Israel.

Rep. Hillary Scholten (D., Mich.) has withheld an endorsement from El-Sayed over his remarks about Israel and his affiliation with Hasan Piker, the socialist influencer who said that "America deserved 9/11" and that Israel is "much worse" than Hamas. State senator Jeremy Moss, a Jewish Democrat, withheld his endorsement from El-Sayed in August after the candidate refused to condemn Piker over the influencer's antisemitic remarks.

State representative Noah Arbit (D.) said he will not back El-Sayed because it is "very clear that the fulcrum of Abdul's campaign was an antisemitic conspiracy about AIPAC being the No. 1 obstacle toward universal healthcare, better schools and better roads in Michigan and in America."

El-Sayed has a lengthy track record of equating Israel with America's adversaries.

At last week's debate against Republican Mike Rogers, El-Sayed sidestepped a question about whether Israel or Iran is a greater threat to America.

"I think both of them have proven dangerous in their own way," El-Sayed said. "One at risk of attacking us. One getting us into wars we have no business fighting."

El-Sayed's remarks are in contrast with those of another Michigan Democrat. Pete Buttigieg, considered a potential 2028 presidential candidate, told Fox News in response to El-Sayed's remarks that "Iran is our enemy, Israel is not, they're an ally."

El-Sayed, who has declined to say whether Israel has a right to exist as a Jewish state, has tried to repair his rocky relationship with Jewish Democrats. He met with Jewish leaders in August and apologized for his remarks after a Hezbollah-inspired attack on Temple Israel outside Detroit on March 12. The assailant, Ayman Ghazali, attacked the synagogue in retaliation for Israel's killing of his brothers, both of whom were members of Hezbollah in southern Lebanon. At the time, El-Sayed stated of the attacker, "Hurt people hurt people."

"I made a mistake" with that remark, El-Sayed told members of the Michigan Democratic Jewish Caucus in August. "I should have issued a statement, of course condemning it, and it just should have been the full stop."

El-Sayed also faced heat at last week's debate for failing to issue a statement on the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks. He said he did not want to take advantage of the anniversary for political purposes.

But El-Sayed issued a statement on the second anniversary of the attack that equated Hamas and Israel. He also sent out a fundraising email that referenced the attack but only mentioned Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu as an aggressor, with no mention of Hamas.

El-Sayed's campaign did not respond to a request for comment.

text:
Psalm 5
 A morning prayer asking for help Those who welcome the Word as the guest of their hearts will have abiding joy.

To my words give ear, O Lord, give heed to my groaning. Attend to the sound of my cries, my King and my God.

It is you whom I invoke, O Lord. In the morning you hear me; in the morning I offer you my prayer, watching and waiting.

You are no God who loves evil; no sinner is your guest. The boastful shall not stand their ground before your face.

You hate all who do evil: you destroy all who lie. The deceitful and bloodthirsty man the Lord detests.

But I through the greatness of your love have access to your house. I bow down before your holy temple, filled with awe.

Lead me, Lord, in your justice, because of those who lie in wait; make clear your way before me.

No truth can be found in their mouths, their heart is all mischief, their throat a wide-open grave, all honey their speech.

All those you protect shall be glad and ring out their joy. You shelter them; in you they rejoice, those who love your name.

It is you who bless the just man, Lord: you surround him with favor as with a shield.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit: — as it was in the beginning, is now, and will be for ever. Amen.

text:
✝️ SPOT 🎯N WITH JOHNNY PRESENTS

🔥 WHAT IF YOU'RE SO BUSY BUILDING A LIFE THAT YOU'VE FORGOTTEN THE GOD WHO GAVE IT TO YOU?

📖 Haggai 1:5 (KJV)

"Now therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts; Consider your ways."

THREE WORDS THAT SHOULD MAKE EVERY CHRISTIAN STOP AND THINK: CONSIDER YOUR WAYS!

We're living in a world where people are working harder, earning more, buying bigger, and staying busier than ever before.

Yet many are spiritually running on empty.

We find time for our jobs, our homes, our hobbies, our entertainment, and our endless scrolling through social media.

BUT HOW OFTEN DOES GOD GET WHATEVER TIME WE HAVE LEFT?

In Haggai's day, God's people had returned from captivity and were busy rebuilding their own lives. Their homes were receiving attention, but the LORD's temple remained neglected.

And God confronted them with a simple but powerful command:

"CONSIDER YOUR WAYS!"

In other words, take a serious look at your priorities!

They were planting, working, earning, and accumulating, yet something was missing.

📖 Haggai 1:6 describes people earning wages only to put them into "a bag with holes."

God was exposing the consequences of their misplaced priorities.

Now, this passage was specifically about Israel's neglect of rebuilding the temple. It doesn't mean every hardship we experience is punishment from God.

But the lesson still speaks loudly today.

YOU CAN HAVE A FULL CALENDAR, A FULL BANK ACCOUNT, AND A FULL HOUSE… YET STILL HAVE A HEART THAT'S STARVING FOR GOD!

Jesus later reminded us:

📖 "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness..." — Matthew 6:33 (KJV)

Notice He didn't say seek Him when it's convenient.

HE SAID SEEK HIM FIRST!

There's nothing wrong with working hard, providing for your family, or enjoying God's blessings.

But there's something terribly wrong when the blessings become more important than the One who provides them.

So here's a question worth asking ourselves today:

AM I BUILDING MY LIFE AROUND GOD, OR AM I TRYING TO FIT GOD INTO THE LIFE I'VE ALREADY BUILT?

Because one day, everything we've accumulated will be left behind.

But our relationship with Jesus Christ has eternal significance.

🔥 DON'T BECOME SO BUSY MAKING A LIVING THAT YOU FORGET WHO GAVE YOU LIFE!

Perhaps the most important thing you can do today isn't to accomplish something else.

It's to stop, open God's Word, bow your head, and sincerely examine your priorities.

GOD ISN'T ASKING FOR A PLACE ON YOUR SCHEDULE. HE DESERVES FIRST PLACE IN YOUR HEART! ❤️✝️

🙏 Lord, forgive us when we put temporary things ahead of eternal ones. Help us examine our hearts, correct our priorities, and seek You first in everything. In Jesus' name, Amen.

---

❤️ ONE FINAL THOUGHT: If you don't know Jesus Christ as your Lord and Savior, no amount of worldly success can replace the salvation He freely offers through faith in Him. (Ephesians 2:8–9)

If this message spoke to your heart, share it. Someone may need this reminder today.

Stay SPOT 🎯N the Word and Keep Walking the Narrow Road! 🎯✝️

All glory, honor, and praise belong to Jesus Christ! 🙌🏻

text:
U.S. Secretary of State James Baker’s February 1990 “not one inch eastward” remark to Gorbachev concerned only the stationing of NATO forces in a reunified Germany (former East Germany), during Two Plus Four talks. It was never a formal commitment about Poland, the Baltics, Ukraine, or any other sovereign state.⁠Globalwatch
No treaty, including the 1990 Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany, contains any such prohibition. Gorbachev himself confirmed in 2014 that “the topic of ‘NATO expansion’ was not discussed at all” beyond Germany.⁠Cepa
NATO’s open-door policy is in Article 10 of the 1949 Washington Treaty. Membership decisions require consensus among Allies and are driven by the applicant countries, not imposed by NATO.
NATO Expansion Was Voluntary and Defensive; Russia Already Borders NATO
Poland, Hungary, Czechia (1999), the Baltics and others (2004), etc., applied because of historical experience with Soviet domination and desire for security guarantees. NATO did not recruit them.
Russia has shared a border with NATO since 1949 (Norway). The Baltic states joined in 2004. Finland’s 2023 accession added roughly 1,300 km of border. Putin explicitly said Russia had “no problems” with Finland and Sweden joining and that it posed “no direct threat.” He has not treated their membership as an existential crisis the way he has treated Ukraine’s aspirations.⁠Politico
Pre-2014, NATO had essentially no permanent combat forces on the territory of new Eastern members. The NATO-Russia Founding Act (1997) included a political (not legally binding) statement of “no intention, no plan and no reason” to station nuclear weapons or substantial permanent combat forces on new members’ territory. Russia later suspended related arms-control commitments.
Timeline Contradicts the Provocation Narrative
Ukraine’s public support for NATO membership was low for years: ~18% in favor and ~67% against in 2013 under Yanukovych (who enshrined non-bloc status). Support rose sharply after Russia’s 2014 seizure of Crimea and intervention in Donbas (to ~48% later that year, then 80%+ after the 2022 full-scale invasion).⁠Statista
At the 2008 Bucharest Summit, NATO said Ukraine and Georgia “will become members” someday but offered no Membership Action Plan and no timetable. Key Allies (Germany, France) blocked faster progress. Ukraine was never close to joining in 2014 or early 2022. German Chancellor Scholz told Putin shortly before the 2022 invasion that Ukrainian membership was off the table for the foreseeable future.
Russia invaded Georgia in 2008 (after Bucharest) and Ukraine in 2014 and 2022 while those countries were not on the verge of NATO entry. Aggression increased Ukrainian desire for NATO, not the other way around.
Russia’s Own Commitments and Putin’s Stated Aims
In the 1994 Budapest Memorandum, Russia (along with the U.S. and UK) pledged to respect Ukraine’s independence, sovereignty, and existing borders in exchange for Ukraine transferring the world’s third-largest nuclear arsenal to Russia and joining the NPT as a non-nuclear state. Russia violated this in 2014 and 2022.⁠Wikisource
Putin’s July 2021 essay “On the Historical Unity of Russians and Ukrainians” argues that Russians and Ukrainians are “one people,” questions the legitimacy of modern Ukraine’s borders, calls independent Ukraine an “anti-Russia project,” and frames the issue in imperial/historical rather than primarily defensive NATO terms. Similar themes appear in his pre-invasion speeches.
Putin has repeatedly framed the conflict around denying Ukraine the right to choose its own alliances and existence as a fully independent state, not around any concrete, imminent NATO attack (none was planned or feasible).
2014 Euromaidan Was Not a Western “Coup”
Protests began after Yanukovych abandoned a long-negotiated EU Association Agreement under Russian pressure and accepted a Russian bailout. They were a mass, largely grassroots movement lasting months.
Yanukovych fled to Russia after his forces killed protesters (the “Heavenly Hundred”). Ukraine’s parliament (Verkhovna Rada), including many from his own Party of Regions, voted (328–0, a constitutional majority) to remove him. Subsequent elections were held. Leaked U.S. diplomatic calls showed interest in outcomes but not orchestration of a coup.⁠Kyivindependent
Additional Points
NATO is a defensive alliance. No NATO member has been invaded by Russia; the pattern of post-Cold War aggression runs the other way (Georgia, Ukraine, and earlier Chechnya/Moldova).
If NATO membership itself were the core threat, Finland’s accession (longer border, no territorial disputes with Russia of the kind Putin claims in Ukraine) would have produced a far stronger reaction. It did not.
Russia’s December 2021 draft treaties demanded a veto over further NATO enlargement and rollback of existing members’ forces—terms that were non-starters and served as a pretext rather than a negotiable security demand.
These points are drawn from primary documents, contemporary statements (including Gorbachev’s and Putin’s), public-opinion data, and timelines from multiple independent sources. The “NATO made him do it” framing inverts cause and effect: Russian military actions against neighbors seeking Western integration have repeatedly strengthened the demand for NATO protection.

text:
Job adverts in Georgia are being used to recruit workers for Russian military contracts, Russian anti-war project 

A Russian anti-war project says job adverts offering work in Tbilisi and Rustavi may be used to recruit people for contracts with Russia’s Defence Ministry, after a man responding to one such advert was offered jobs in a Russia-occupied Ukrainian region and Russia instead.

The man contacted Get Lost (Идите лесом), a project that helps Russians avoid military conscription and assists soldiers seeking to leave the army. (Founded in 2022 by Russian anti-war activist Grigory Sverdlin, the project provides legal and psychological support to people who do not want to take part in the war against Ukraine.) 

According to the project, the man found an advert in a Tbilisi jobs chat seeking manual labourers for work in the Georgian capital and Rustavi. The offer promised 200 lari ($74) a day, free accommodation, three meals and a six-day working week.

He responded, presenting himself as a candidate with construction experience. But recruiter told him that the positions in Georgia had already been filled and offered him work as a communications specialist or security guard in the Russian-occupied Kherson region of Ukraine or Russia’s Belgorod region.

The recruiter said the jobs were officially based in Russia and offered a monthly salary of 170,000 to 210,000 roubles (approximately $1,900–$2,350), advance payments every 10 days and a free flight from Tbilisi to Moscow.

The candidate was asked to send a copy of his passport. A logistics worker would then arrange his journey to the job location.

The key condition emerged later: the candidate would have to sign a contract with Russia’s Defence Ministry.

“We will have two contracts. First, I want to tell you: one with us, the other with the Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation,” the recruiter told him, according to messages published by Get Lost.

She reportedly explained that the military contract was necessary to obtain “licences” to work in border areas.

The recruiter also sent sample employment agreements for temporary migrant workers. The documents named a private security company, OFBR, and listed positions including security guard and communications specialist.

The agreements promised free accommodation, travel expenses and medical care. However, they also stipulated that workers who terminated their contracts early would have to reimburse the employer for expenses incurred on their behalf or work off the amount owed.

The recruiter did not mention any one-off payment for signing a contract with the Russian Defence Ministry, the project said.

The man declined the offer and shared his correspondence, voice messages and copies of the contracts with Get Lost.

On 18 October, he found a similar advert on another platform, again offering manual labour jobs in Tbilisi and Rustavi for 200 lari a day. The contact listed was the same Telegram account, according to the project.

Get Lost said it had received 13 requests for assistance in September from foreign nationals serving under Russian military contracts and their relatives. Between 1 and 13 October, it received another 10 requests concerning recruitment through job adverts on the Russian classifieds platform Avito and offers of rotational work.

Russia’s invasion of Ukraine has been accompanied by repeated efforts to recruit personnel for its armed forces, including through financial incentives and contract service. The case described by Get Lost suggests that jobseekers abroad may also be approached through offers initially presented as civilian employment.
